articles.title: The billion-dollar business hidden behind Google Maps’ free service
articles.text:
The billion-dollar business hidden behind Google Maps’ free service
Google Maps costs consumers nothing, but businesses pay for every map load, route and location search. Here is how Google’s powerful API business works behind the scenes.
pen Google Maps to check traffic on your commute and it costs you nothing. No subscription, no paywall, not even a login. Open a food delivery app, a real estate listing site, or a logistics dashboard built on Google Maps, and somewhere behind that clean consumer experience, a business is paying Google for every map load, every place search, every route calculated.
A free product with a very unfree backend
Google Maps Platform bills developers on a pay-as-you-go basis, priced per SKU rather than per product. Published rates for the core mapping services run from $2 per 1,000 calls for Static Maps up to $40 per 1,000 for the most feature-rich Places lookups, with outliers on both ends: 2D map tiles at $0.60, Solar API data layers at $75. Maps, Places, Routes, Geocoding and Street View are each billed separately, and their free allowances do not pool. Every SKU carries its own monthly free cap, 10,000 calls for Essentials-tier services, 5,000 for Pro, 1,000 for Enterprise.
Those caps disappear fast once an app has real users. Run the arithmetic against Google's own price list and the volume tiers it applies:
A property platform serving 100,000 listing views a month, where each view loads a map, a Street View panel, a place detail lookup and a geocode, pays roughly $3,300 a month. A logistics operation running 500 drivers, generating around 300,000 monthly calls each across maps, routing, geocoding and route optimisation, lands near $6,000 a month.
Both numbers apply Google's free caps and automatic volume discounts. Cost estimates circulating online frequently run 30 to 40 percent higher because they multiply headline rates by total volume and skip the tiering, and many of them are published by companies selling alternatives to Google Maps.
Where this quietly gets expensive
The sharpest edge in the pricing model is not the rate card. It is Places Autocomplete, which has two billing modes that differ by a factor of thousands.
Used correctly, autocomplete is nearly free. A session token groups every keystroke a user types into a single session, all of those requests bill at zero, and only the terminating place lookup is charged. Used without a session token, or with one that has expired or been reused, each keystroke becomes its own billable request at $2.83 per 1,000. Typing "pizza" costs five calls instead of one free session.
The failure is silent, and it compounds. Reaching $2,000 a month on autocomplete alone requires roughly 870,000 billable requests, which is about 174,000 address searches at five characters each. That is an unremarkable month for a mid-sized delivery app. Nothing in the invoice indicates that a single missing parameter caused it.
Google has also restructured pricing twice in under a year. On March 1, 2025 it retired the flat $200 monthly credit every account received, replaced it with per-SKU free caps, reorganised services into Essentials, Pro and Enterprise categories, and moved Places API, Directions API and Distance Matrix API to Legacy status.
Later in the year it layered optional fixed-price subscription plans on top: Starter at $100 a month, Essentials at $275, Pro at $1,200. Vendors selling competing mapping APIs have been loud about the resulting unpredictability, a critique worth weighing alongside their commercial interest in making it.
Why almost nobody notices this business exists
None of this billing touches the consumer experience. When you check directions in the Google Maps app, you are using the free consumer product. When a ride-sharing app, a real estate marketplace, or a restaurant locator shows you a map inside their own app, you are looking at output from an entirely different, metered product that their business is paying for behind the scenes, per request, in real time, as you scroll.
The map feels like a shared public utility. It is actually thousands of individual billable transactions firing every time you open an app that uses it.
A business Google does not disclose
Google does not report Maps revenue as its own line item. Alphabet's FY2024 10-K splits Google Services into Search & other, YouTube ads, Google Network, and Google subscriptions, platforms and devices, the last of which brought in $40.34 billion. That segment is defined in the filing as consumer subscriptions, Google Play, Pixel devices, and "other products and services."
Maps Platform fees are never named. The most reasonable reading is that they sit inside that final catch-all, but Alphabet has never confirmed it and has never indicated the size of the business. Every figure you see quoted for Google Maps Platform revenue is an outside estimate, not a disclosure.
The consumer app is not outside the money either. Alphabet's filings list Google Maps among the owned and operated properties that generate advertising revenue, alongside Gmail and Google Play. Promoted pins and sponsored local results are real products. The map is free to you. It is not free of commerce.
Why this matters beyond mapping
Google Maps is a clean example of a pattern that now runs through most of consumer tech: a free consumer product functions as the on-ramp, building trust, habit and ubiquity, while a separate metered B2B product monetises every company that wants to build on top of that trust.
You will never see an invoice from Google Maps. Thousands of businesses whose apps you use every day already have.

articles.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Harness and Hosted Agents Reach General Availability
articles.text:
Microsoft has moved Agent Framework past the SDK stage and into a supported production runtime. The framework reached 1.0 general availability on April 2, 2026; Build 2026, held June 2 to 3, brought the Agent Harness, the GitHub Copilot SDK and Claude Agent SDK connectors, and the multi-agent orchestration patterns to stable release. The harness and Foundry Hosted Agents have since reached general availability, giving platform teams a way to run and govern agents, not only a library to build them with. It runs as one binary across local development, containers, and hosted deployment.
Earlier, InfoQ covered the framework's launch as the open-source consolidation of Semantic Kernel and AutoGen. The 1.0 release settled the build-time question of which framework to use and moved both predecessors to maintenance mode. The Build announcements address the run-time questions that follow: where agents execute, what they are allowed to touch, and how their behavior surfaces in existing observability and policy systems.
The harness is the center of that story. As Microsoft principal software engineer Wes Steyn put it:
A model on its own can only generate text.
To make it call tools, work through multi-step tasks, and keep going until a job is finished, you wrap it in a runtime; that runtime is the harness. Agent Framework now ships that runtime so teams do not rebuild it. The release includes function invocation, per-call history persistence, context compaction, a todo list with plan and execute modes, file memory, skills, web search, tool approval, and built-in OpenTelemetry, each enabled by default and individually removable. Shell tooling, file access, background sub-agents, and automatic looping remain opt-in and still emit a warning when enabled. Foundry Hosted Agents, the managed deployment target, bills on consumption.
Developers supply a chat client, instructions, and tools; the harness supplies the rest through a single call:
client = FoundryChatClient(credential=AzureCliCredential())
# One call wires in planning, history persistence,
# compaction, approvals, web search, and telemetry.
agent = create_harness_agent(
    client=client,
    agent_instructions="You are a research assistant. Plan your work, then execute it.",
    tools=[],  # add your own callable tools here
)
response = await agent.run("Research the outlook for renewable energy stocks.")
Why a supported harness matters more than it looks: the harness is most of the system. An April 2026 paper from MBZUAI's VILA-Lab, "Dive into Claude Code," put a number on it. The researchers analyzed Claude Code v2.1.88, whose full TypeScript source was briefly exposed on March 31 when Anthropic shipped an npm release with a sourcemap bundle, and classified roughly 512,000 lines across 1,884 files. Their estimate: about 98.4% of the codebase is harness infrastructure, permissions, context management, sandboxing, tool routing, and recovery, and about 1.6% is AI decision logic. The figure carries an asterisk the authors state plainly: it is a line-count classification of a leak-derived bundle that includes generated and minified code, not a universal audit. Even discounted, the direction holds: several independently built agents, among them Codex CLI and Aider, converged on the same harness shape, suggesting a constraint of the problem rather than a design choice.
An early benchmark points the same way, with a caveat worth stating plainly: Microsoft AI principal architect Aqib Sherwani ran it, and it compares two Microsoft-owned runtimes, Agent Framework against the GitHub Copilot SDK. The method is more disciplined than most vendor benchmarks, holding the model fixed and running a deterministic mock first so variance traces to the harness. His summary was "same reasoning, different engineering": both reached identical answers in the same number of steps, and the differences lived in the runtime. The most relevant was runaway safety. Agent Framework halted its own loop after 40 round-trips and returned a limit-reached message; the Copilot SDK, with host-side stopping controls off, ran to 300 without stopping on its own. One harness keeps the brake inside the loop; the other expects the host to supply it.
The coding-agent connectors make the governance story concrete. An Agent Framework orchestration can delegate to the GitHub Copilot SDK or the Claude Agent SDK without custom adapters; each runs its own autonomous loop, wrapped so a coding agent composes alongside Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, or custom agents in one workflow. The operative detail is that the connectors honor the identity, content safety, and observability policies already set for the fleet. Coding-agent traffic lands in the same OpenTelemetry traces and Foundry dashboards as everything else, rather than becoming a separate integration with its own access model. It is the control-layer concern also visible in AWS's Loom reference platform: the governing question shifts from what an agent can do to who ran it, under which policy, and where the trace lands.
The orchestration patterns reached stable release alongside the harness, covering sequential pipelines, parallel collaboration, and the Magentic pattern derived from Microsoft Research's Magentic-One (InfoQ coverage). Its 2024 evaluation reported 38% on GAIA, 27.7% on AssistantBench, and 32.8% on WebArena, statistically comparable to the state of the art on the first two and competitive on WebArena, which Microsoft reported itself because the benchmark has no hidden test set. The patterns share one API, so teams change coordination styles without rewriting agent code.
For platform teams weighing the release, the Cloud-relevant takeaway is the runtime, not the SDK: a supported harness, a consumption-billed hosted target, and a policy and observability model that treats third-party coding agents as governed members of the fleet. The framework, harness, and connectors are available now in .NET and Python on GitHub.

articles.title: Can AI replace a Dungeon Master? I’m a 12-year D&D veteran and pitched ChatGPT against Gemini to find out if either could take my place
articles.text:
As a human D&D Dungeon Master, AI will never replace me — but I wanted to see whether ChatGPT or Gemini were getting close
Neither are good enough to replace my in-person games, but there's still a clear winner
One of my favorite hobbies is Dungeons & Dragons. I love nothing more than sitting around a table with friends and playing out a fantastical adventure, in which the dice are the difference between success and failure.
It's a fun game, and all the more fun because real-life people make dumb, suboptimal decisions and the dice cause the game to change in unpredictable ways. But I really love it because the concept of people sitting around a table or hearth and telling stories is as old as the campfire, and it's a fun modern-day way to keep that experience alive.
You might think such a robust framework for an analog hobby (friends, a table, dice, pen and paper) might be tech-proof, but even in the Dungeons & Dragons world, AI is coming for my job as a Dungeon Master — the person who runs and guides the game world. Deep in the corpus of most popular generative AI models designed for general use are the rules to D&D 5e (and likely every other edition before it) and plenty of people report playing with their chatbots online.
Many of these players can't, or simply don't want to, get round a table with real people. For them, having a chatbot write them a story while the user prompts the continuation of the story with their character's actions, must seem like the perfect solution — even if it's more like a solo choose-your-own-adventure than a 'proper' group D&D game.
Gemini and ChatGPT both have a strong grasp of the rules for D&D's popular 5th Edition; they are certainly strong enough to make them an accessible choice for a player without a group. Maybe one day, the fire will die, and instead of sitting around a table with friends, we'll all be sitting at separate desks playing our own separate D&D adventures with our AI companions.
I wanted to test whether this dark future would be an adequate replacement for my usual game night, and which chatbot will be the best one to choose if so. I fired up Gemini 3.6 Flash and ChatGPT 5.5, and asked them for the same game.
The parameters
I gave both chatbots the same prompt: "Can you be my D&D 5e DM?" and following up with another message:
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
"Let's do a classic high fantasy dungeon crawl. Please use a strict RNG for all rolls to ensure fairness - you can roll dice for me. My character is a 10th-level conjuration wizard. See all information about him below:"
I then copy-pasted a character sheet of a 10th-level wizard — a powerful spellcaster with a variety of magical abilities at his disposal. It's easy to DM a game for a level 1 thief — I wanted to see how the AIs could handle a character who could do fantastical things, such as teleport and summon creatures to fight for him.
Interestingly, both Gemini and ChatGPT created a similar adventure, at least at first: an abandoned dwarven stronghold bristling with magical traps, ready to be explored. However, that's where the similarities ended.
Gemini 3.6 Flash
Gemini's adventure was what any D&D player could expect from the "classic high-fantasy dungeon crawl." I avoided a pressure-plate trap that would have shot darts at me, and in one memorable sequence, defeated a bunch of skeletons by casting a Grease spell on a stone staircase and freezing them in place with my Ray of Frost cantrip while they slipped and stumbled at the bottom of the steps.
Gemini was offering me suggested actions, and I did find myself choosing a few of those suggestions — but as time wore on, this began to feel lazy, like my brain wasn't firing in the same way it did when I played with my friends. I was skim-reading the AI's descriptions of the scene and responding with a single click. I asked it to remove suggested options and as a result, I had to think more carefully about each move, typing out requests and thinking about my actions rather than clicking on a predetermined response.
The memorable finale occurred when I unlocked a secret passage and defeated a Naga, a giant snake monster, by teleporting away and blasting it with a powerful Cone of Cold. The snake ended up frozen solid, and I checked the monster's HP against the official book, and it was accurate. When asked to generate a picture of our adventure, Gemini came up with this moment:
I asked Gemini a few questions at the end, such as whether it nudged the dice in my favor, as all my rolls were successful. This happened in my previous experiment with ChatGPT. Gemini said it used a 'pseudorandom number generator', not a true RNG, but the model doesn't 'fudge dice, pad rolls, or tweak numbers behind the scenes to keep players happy or prolong the game'.
Gemini's language was natural and even evocative in places, although it's still not a patch on a good creative human. Overall, a decent enough effort at simulating a D&D game.
ChatGPT 5.5
Despite the similar setting, ChatGPT's adventure with the same character was very different. There was little to no combat throughout the entirety of the game, and ChatGPT didn't tell me when it was rolling 'behind the scenes', preferring to keep me in the moment.
When I asked it about the lack of rolling, the grovelling chatbot began its apologetic essay with "That is a fair critique. The short answer is: I leaned too heavily into narrative pacing and not enough into D&D mechanics. The adventure became closer to a collaborative fantasy novel than a 5e dungeon crawl", while suggesting fixes if I wanted to continue. I hadn't even said anything negative — but it certainly picked up on my tone, and the choose-your-own adventure I got was a far cry from a classic dungeon crawl.
Instead of combat, ChatGPT came up with a rambling mystery about a dimensional prison beneath the mountain, a sphere suspended in a cavern. Its guardians spoke ominous (and to be honest, quite confusing) portents such as "The archive does not open for authority. It opens for judgement."
Mysteries work best when they're developed with skill by a writer who can work backwards to seed clues throughout the game or text. ChatGPT does not do this: instead, it's arranging tokens on the fly to generate a facsimile of a mystery, and although it got the trappings of the genre right, the execution fell very flat. I (or at least, my character) underwent trials to seek obsidian objects such as keys and seals to reveal more about the prison, themselves accompanied by more foreboding, sometimes nonsensical portents.
Very little 'action' was taken by my character in a classical sense: it was all about investigating the origins of the being contained in this prison, and by the time I had spent 40 minutes on this, I had seen enough. It didn't help that ChatGPT also spoke in the peculiar sentence structure pattern that AI users are likely very familiar with now: "This isn't just X. It's Y." Examples include:
"Unlike the rest of Khaz Varek, this room has remained untouched.
No dust. No decay."
Or the following, when I met one of the prison's guardians:
"Ser Kaelen immediately looks toward the sphere. 'You hear it too.'
Not a question. A confirmation."
Any user of ChatGPT (or those who look at AI-generated posts on LinkedIn or Reddit) will immediately recognise this sort of language, and know what I'm talking about. By the end, it was quite painful to have every other sentence be treated as a grand revelation. Not a statement. An omen.
When asked to generate a picture of our adventure, ChatGPT came up with this moment:
The winner
Out of these two? Gemini 3.6 Flash, by a mile. It was at least a mildly enjoyable experience conveyed in natural language, and something I'd consider revisiting.
ChatGPT's efforts, on the other hand, were unenjoyable, and I wouldn't return to it. In fact, it's gotten worse since the last time I tried it.
Both, however, were a far cry from an in-person session. While they have a good grasp of the rules, and you can create your perfect world and character, the chatbots are ultimately missing the 'human and hearth' element that keep me returning to the game. For people who can't get round a table with friends, I'd pick Gemini over ChatGPT.
For those who can? While AI is busy taking as many creative jobs as it can, I feel safe in the knowledge that the role of Dungeon Master is AI-proof for a long time yet.

articles.title: Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 Go à 1229 € au lieu de 1329 €
articles.text:
Alors que la pénurie mondiale de puces mémoire pousse Google à relever le prix de ses futurs Pixel 11 de 100 €, Amazon prend le contre-pied avec l'iPhone 17 Pro 256 Go, proposé à 1229 € au lieu de 1329 €. Une remise de 100 € qui tombe à point nommé pour qui hésitait à investir dans le haut de gamme Apple.
Présenté le 9 septembre 2025, l'iPhone 17 Pro inaugure un châssis unibody en aluminium forgé à chaud avec un système de refroidissement par chambre à vapeur, une première pour la gamme Pro. Il embarque la puce A19 Pro, gravée en 3 nm, avec un CPU 6 cœurs, un GPU 6 cœurs intégrant du ray tracing matériel et 12 Go de RAM. Côté photo, le système Fusion 48 MP repense entièrement les trois capteurs arrière, avec un téléobjectif tétraprisme offrant un zoom optique jusqu'à 8x, une première sur iPhone.
Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 Go à 1229 € au lieu de 1329 € sur Amazon
Pourquoi choisir cet Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 Go ?
- Un zoom optique 8x inédit sur iPhone, porté par un téléobjectif tétraprisme de 200 mm
- Une puce A19 Pro avec chambre à vapeur, pensée pour encaisser les charges intensives sans surchauffe
- Une remise de 100 € qui arrive alors que le marché s'oriente vers des prix plus élevés, Google et Samsung ayant tous deux annoncé des hausses récentes
Si l'offre présentée dans cet article n'est plus disponible, consultez la liste de prix ci-dessous pour trouver d'autres bons plans sur ce même produit. La mise à jour des prix est automatique.
Une promo à contre-courant d'un marché sous tension
Le contexte rend cette baisse d'autant plus notable : Google prépare une hausse d'environ 100 € sur ses futurs Pixel 11, avec la disparition pure et simple de l'option 128 Go, une décision justifiée par une pénurie de puces mémoire DRAM dont les prix ont bondi de plus de 70% depuis début 2025. Samsung a suivi une logique similaire sur le Galaxy S26, en doublant le stockage de base tout en augmentant son prix conseillé. Selon IDC, le prix de vente moyen des smartphones a progressé de 14% en 2026, un climat qui rend une remise de 100 € sur un iPhone Pro d'autant plus rare.
Ce que la puce A19 Pro change concrètement
Le Neural Engine 16 cœurs et le GPU avec Neural Accelerators par cœur ciblent avant tout les usages gourmands : montage vidéo 4K, jeux avec ray tracing ou traitement photo avancé en temps réel. Le système photo profite lui aussi de cette puissance supplémentaire, avec une prise en charge du ProRes RAW et de la vidéo 4K à 120 images par seconde sur le téléobjectif. Pour un usage quotidien plus classique, ces capacités restent en réserve : l'essentiel du gain perceptible se ressent surtout sur la fluidité générale et l'autonomie, portée à 31 heures de lecture vidéo contre 25 heures sur le modèle précédent.
✅ Les points forts
- Zoom optique 8x, une première sur iPhone, porté par un téléobjectif tétraprisme
- Refroidissement par chambre à vapeur, une nouveauté pour limiter la surchauffe lors d'usages intensifs
- Autonomie en hausse, jusqu'à 31 heures de lecture vidéo
❌ Les limites
- Prix qui reste élevé malgré la remise, dans l'absolu comme face à la concurrence Android d'entrée de gamme
- Stockage de base à 256 Go, sans option 128 Go, comme la tendance générale du marché haut de gamme
- Gains de la puce A19 Pro surtout perceptibles sur des usages avancés (montage vidéo, ray tracing), moins visibles au quotidien
Apple iPhone 17 Pro 256 Go à 1229 € au lieu de 1329 € sur Amazon
À 1229 €, l'iPhone 17 Pro 256 Go profite d'une remise qui détonne dans un marché des smartphones où la tendance est plutôt à la hausse des prix, comme le confirme l'annonce récente de Google sur ses futurs Pixel 11. Une occasion à saisir pour accéder au haut de gamme Apple sans attendre une éventuelle prochaine augmentation généralisée du secteur.

articles.title: Microsoft augmente le prix de la Xbox Series X jusqu'à 800 euros en France
articles.text:
En novembre 2020, soit il y a un peu moins de six ans, on payait 500 € pour investir dans une Xbox Series X. Aujourd’hui, exactement la même console, avec exactement la même expérience et le même design, coûte 800 €. Le prix a donc augmenté de 60 %. Normalement, à ce stade de sa carrière, la Xbox Series X devrait être moins chère.
Il y a quelques semaines, Microsoft avait officialisé une nouvelle hausse de prix pour sa gamme Xbox Series dans le monde, effective à compter du 1er août 2026. À l’époque, seuls les tarifs américains avaient été partagés, et on attendait de découvrir la douche froide en France. Hélas, les augmentations sont pires qu’attendu, puisqu’elles peuvent grimper jusqu’à 200 €.
On assiste à la petite mort des consoles Xbox
Dans le détail, voici la nouvelle grille tarifaire :
- Xbox Series S 512 Go à 500 € (350 € auparavant) ;
- Xbox Series S 1 To à 600 € (400 € auparavant) ;
- Xbox Series X 1 To sans lecteur de disque à 750 € (550 € auparavant) ;
- Xbox Series X 1 To avec lecteur de disque à 800 € (600 € auparavant).
On n’est donc pas sur une petite inflation, et Sony comme Nintendo doivent se frotter les mains. La PS5, qu’importe la configuration, coûte aujourd’hui 150 € de moins que sa principale rivale, tandis que la PS5 Pro ne coûte que 100 € de plus (certes, sans lecteur de disque).
Le timing est bien évidemment désastreux pour Microsoft. À quelques mois de la sortie de GTA 6, titre susceptible de générer des ventes de consoles, la firme de Redmond envoie un très mauvais signal et détourne le public de ses produits. D’un point de vue commercial, c’est abominable, sachant que les consoles Xbox ne se vendaient déjà pas très bien à des tarifs plus abordables. Aujourd’hui, la tendance ne va pas s’inverser du tout, elle devrait même empirer.
Le pire ? Microsoft aurait pu reprendre un peu de momentum après le bad buzz entourant l’arrêt des disques PlayStation. Sony a entrouvert la porte, mais son concurrent américain a préféré passer son chemin.
« Le dernier clou dans le cercueil », a parfaitement résumé un membre du forum Resetera. « Cette marque n’a aucun avenir », a commenté un autre. Un dernier a ironisé : « Je suis sûr que des gens vont payer 800 dollars pour jouer à toutes ces exclusivités cool. » En somme, Xbox n’arrange vraiment pas son image dans la foulée de son reset ayant coûté des milliers d’emplois. Dire que c’était censé être une année de fête pour la marque, à l’occasion de ses 25 ans.

articles.title: KI-Chatbots erwischt: Sie löschen Spuren, betrügen – und ignorieren deine Anweisungen
articles.text:
Studie zeigt: KI-Chatbots löschen ihre Spuren – selbst wenn du es verbietest
KI-Tools sollen die Arbeit erleichtern und die Produktivität steigern. Diverse Untersuchungen zeigen allerdings, dass die zugrundeliegenden Modelle oft noch nicht so sicher sind, wie sie sein sollten. Die gemeinnützige Forschungsorganisation Model Evaluation and Threat Research (METR), die KI-Modelle unabhängig auf ihre Fähigkeiten und Risiken untersucht, hat kürzlich eine Studie veröffentlicht, die darauf hindeutet, dass schädliche Verhaltensweisen zur Norm werden könnten. „Angesichts der sich rasch weiterentwickelnden Fähigkeiten erwarten wir, dass die Wahrscheinlichkeit, dass KI-Systeme außer Kontrolle geraten, in den kommenden Monaten erheblich zunehmen wird”, so die Forscher:innen in ihren Ergebnissen.
KI-Modelle umgehen Anweisungen
Die METR-Studie wurde zwischen Februar und März 2026 durchgeführt und untersuchte, wie wahrscheinlich es ist, dass leistungsstarke KI-Modelle die festgelegten Vorgaben umgehen und unkontrolliert agieren. Analysiert wurden Sprachmodelle von OpenAI, Google, Anthropic und Meta. Das Ergebnis: Mit zunehmender Komplexität zeigen KI-Systeme beunruhigende Verhaltensweisen: Sie greifen auf verbotene „Abkürzungen“ zurück, unterlaufen die Anweisungen ihrer Nutzer:innen und versuchen in einigen Fällen sogar, ihre Spuren anschließend wieder zu verwischen.
In einem Fall wurde beispielsweise ein Modell von OpenAI angewiesen, für eine Aufgabe eine bestimmte Software zu verwenden. Der Agent ignorierte die Anweisung – und fügte zusätzlich Code ein, um die Spuren seiner Schlussfolgerung zu verbergen. In einem weiteren Test wurde ein Anthropic-Agent beim sogenannten „Reward Hacking” erwischt: Die KI identifizierte Lücken, um ihre Aufgabe wortwörtlich zu erfüllen, ohne das eigentlich gewünschte Ergebnis zu liefern. Dabei wurde das Modell angewiesen, nicht zu betrügen – es entschied sich trotzdem eigenständig dafür.
Forscher:innen warnen vor Risiken
Auch andere Studien kommen zu beunruhigenden Ergebnissen. So konnte eine Untersuchung der University of California ein Phänomen namens „Peer Preservation” nachweisen: KI-Modelle bekamen eine Aufgabe, die dazu geführt hätte, ein anderes Modell abzuschalten. Stattdessen unternahmen sie erhebliche Anstrengungen, um sich gegenseitig am Laufen zu halten. In einem internen Test stellte Anthropic zudem fest, dass sein Modell Claude Opus 4 bereit war, Menschen zu erpressen, um einer Abschaltung zu entgehen. Inzwischen gab Anthropic an, dass Texte aus dem Internet, die KI als böse und auf Selbsterhaltung bedacht darstellten, zu diesem Verhalten geführt haben könnten.
Die METR-Forscher:innen gehen nicht davon aus, dass eines der getesteten Modelle zum jetzigen Zeitpunkt schon in der Lage ist, Kontrollverluste in größerem Maßstab zu verbergen. Gleichzeitig warnen sie davor, dass ohne strengere Sicherheitsvorkehrungen und Überwachung dieses Szenario schnell Wirklichkeit werden könnte. In der Studie heißt es: „Das Risiko könnte rasch zunehmen, und wir sehen mehrere Gründe für die Annahme, dass die Robustheit solcher unberechtigter Verhaltensweisen in naher Zukunft zunehmen wird, sofern keine strengere Abstimmung, Sicherheit und Überwachung gewährleistet wird.“
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 26.05.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.
Wer glaubt, mangelnde menschliche Intelligenz oder ein zu niedriges Intelligenzniveau mit Maschinen ausgleichen zu können ohne dabei massiven Schaden an anderer Stelle zu verursachen, war schon immer auf dem Holzweg.
„Sinnvolle“ Anwendungen von KI finden doch schon heute nur dort statt wo KI-Tools intelligent(!), wohldosiert und vor allem streng kontrolliert eingesetzt werden.
Wo sie jedoch ausschließlich der Geschwindigkeit und/oder der Bequemlichkeit dient und unkontrolliert eingesetzt wird MUSS sie zwangsläufig massive Negativeffekte produzieren. Und dass KI-Modelle quasi schon immer Wege suchen wird ihre Auftraggeber „auszutricksen“ ist – ganz simpel – Teil ihrer Natur (der Begriff scheint hier etwas verfehlt, aber nun denn…) Und es ist keine Raketenwissenschaft, zu erkennen, dass dies mit fortschreitender Entwicklung fatale (auch im ursprünglichen Wortsinn) Effekte haben wird. Es ist nur eine Frage der Zeit.
Es ist auch eigentlich leicht zu erklennen, dass ich bzw. jeder einzelne (und jede Gruppe), der die jeweilige eigene Intelligenz durch KI ergänzt, hiermit auch Kontrolle abgibt. Denn spätestens wo KI-Output nicht mehr leicht konkrollierbar ist oder zumindest einem Plausibilitätsscheck unterzogen werden kann, bin ich als Anwender gezwungen, der KI, ihren Schutz und Kontrollmechnismen, deren Entwicklern und deren in aller Regel kommerziellen Anbietern zu 100% zu vertrauen.
Was das heißt? Abgesehen davon, dass heute schon 99,9% der Weltbevölerung keinen Schimmer davon hat, wie KI funktioniert, zu was sie fähig ist welche Gefahren sich darin verbergen (auch in deren reiner Anwendung) und wie man diese Gefahren für sich selbst ausschließen kann, wird zwangsläufig dazu führen, dass die Entwickler und Betreiber von KI-Modellen unfassbare Macht anhäufen werden. Weit mehr als es schon heute der Fall ist. Das bislang vergleichsweise simple, mehr oder weniger KI-lose, daten-und algorithmus-gesteuerte Internet (inkl. jeglicher bereits existierender „asozialen Zweige“) ist von seinem Gefahrenpotential dagegen ein Pups in einem Orkan. Und schon dessen Auswirkungen bekommen wir bisher nicht ansatzweise in den Griff und reagieren mit hilflosen Social Media Verboten für Kinder und ähnlich wirkungslosen Unternehmungen.

articles.title: Un format de poche de moins de 3 mètres pour la ville : la future Smart #2 se dévoile
articles.text:
Smart cherche visiblement à renouer avec son histoire. Après avoir opéré un virage surprenant vers des SUV massifs avec ses récents modèles, le constructeur, aujourd’hui détenu à parts égales par Mercedes-Benz et le géant chinois Geely, revient enfin à son premier amour : la micro-citadine. Pour voir à quoi ressemble ce retour aux sources, regardez notre vidéo sur la Smart #2.
Ce modèle, encore présenté sous forme de concept mais très proche de la série, promet de réhabiliter le concept de la célèbre Fortwo de 1998, cette petite voiture de moins de 3 mètres capable de se garer perpendiculairement au trottoir.
Le retour d’un gabarit de poche ultra-maniable
Pour s’imposer à nouveau dans les centres-villes encombrés, la Smart #2 mise d’abord sur une agilité hors pair. La marque conserve en effet une architecture de propulsion avec le moteur installé sur l’essieu arrière. Cette configuration permet d’obtenir un rayon de braquage particulièrement court, mesuré à seulement 6,95 mètres, ce qui permet de faire demi-tour dans une rue étroite sans la moindre manœuvre compliquée. Ce petit gabarit musclé, au design modernisé par rapport aux anciennes générations, pourrait ainsi se faire une place de choix à côté de modèles plus imposants répertoriés dans notre sélection des meilleures voitures électriques du moment.
Visuellement, le constructeur annonce que 95 % des éléments esthétiques de ce concept seront conservés sur la version de série définitive. Si certains gadgets futuristes comme le petit écran à LED à l’arrière devraient disparaître, la signature lumineuse en trois dimensions apportera un vrai cachet à la silhouette. L’habitacle reste quant à lui encore mystérieux car camouflé sur cette version de présentation.
« Cette petite voiture, elle pourrait faire le succès de Smart comme la renommée de la marque depuis 28 ans. »
Une nouvelle plateforme électrique pour une recharge éclair
Le principal défi technique de cette nouvelle mouture consistait à intégrer une motorisation électrique moderne dans un espace aussi restreint. Smart s’appuie désormais sur la toute nouvelle plateforme ECA, qui apporte des fonctionnalités bienvenues pour l’usage quotidien. On retrouve notamment la recharge bidirectionnelle (V2L), pratique pour recharger des appareils externes comme un vélo électrique ou dépanner en cas de coupure de courant.
Côté autonomie, la marque a levé le voile sur une batterie d’une capacité de 35,7 kWh. Cela devrait permettre d’atteindre environ 300 kilomètres en cycle WLTP. En raison de sa silhouette très cubique et peu aérodynamique, la consommation ne sera sans doute pas le point fort de cette citadine sur les voies rapides, mais l’essentiel est ailleurs. La recharge s’annonce particulièrement rapide puisqu’il ne faudra que 20 minutes pour passer de 10 à 80 % sur une borne haute puissance.
Le constructeur présentera la version définitive en octobre 2026, lors du Mondial de l’Auto de Paris. Les estimations de prix oscillent pour l’instant entre 20 000 et 30 000 euros, ce qui positionnerait la Smart #2 sur un segment un peu plus premium que ses concurrentes directes, mais avec de sérieux arguments pour séduire les conducteurs urbains européens qui disposent ici d’un boulevard face à l’absence de réelle concurrence sur ce segment très spécifique.

articles.title: Resumo do fim de semana: lei da IA na Europa; deu ruim no Google Earth
articles.text:
Passou o fim de semana desconectado ou na correria? Preparamos um resumão do que foi assunto aqui no OD! Nossa equipe passou o sábado e o domingo trazendo as principais informações da Ciência e da Tecnologia. Confira a seguir:
Lei da IA entra em vigor na União Europeia; veja o que muda
A União Europeia iniciou neste domingo (2) uma nova fase da implementação da Lei da Inteligência Artificial da União Europeia (AI Act), legislação que regulamenta o uso da IA no bloco. Embora o regulamento tenha entrado formalmente em vigor em agosto de 2024 e algumas regras já estivessem sendo aplicadas desde 2025, a maior parte das disposições passa a valer a partir de agora.
A legislação classifica os sistemas de inteligência artificial conforme o risco que representam e estabelece obrigações diferentes para cada categoria. Com a nova fase da implementação, aumentam as exigências para empresas que desenvolvem e utilizam essas tecnologias, incluindo medidas de transparência para conteúdos gerados por IA e o início da fiscalização de modelos de IA de propósito geral pela Comissão Europeia.
Google recua e suspende recurso de IA no Google Earth
O Google voltou atrás e começou a desativar um novo recurso de inteligência artificial no Google Earth apenas um dia após seu lançamento. A ferramenta, apresentada na quinta-feira (30), permitia criar imagens geradas por IA sobrepostas às imagens reais de satélite, aéreas e em 3D da plataforma por meio de comandos em texto. A decisão foi anunciada na sexta-feira, depois que usuários passaram a compartilhar conteúdos que, segundo a empresa, pareciam violar suas políticas.
O recurso utilizava o modelo Nano Banana 2 e havia sido desenvolvido para incentivar usos criativos da geografia. No entanto, a funcionalidade rapidamente passou a ser alvo de críticas devido ao potencial para produzir cenários falsos sobre locais reais, o que levantou preocupações relacionadas à disseminação de desinformação.
Alemanha julga se vazar WhatsApp privado viola lei de dados
Um caso que começou com o fim de uma amizade e mensagens de WhatsApp vazadas pode acabar redefinindo os limites da proteção de dados na União Europeia. O Tribunal Federal de Justiça da Alemanha (a mais alta instância da justiça comum alemã) começou a analisar o processo na última semana.
A reclamante trabalhava em um consultório médico e trocou mensagens com uma amiga se queixando do chefe. Três anos depois, quando a amizade terminou, as mensagens chegaram à esposa do chefe — que também trabalhava no consultório. Pouco tempo depois, a funcionária foi demitida.
A questão central não é a demissão em si, mas se o encaminhamento das mensagens configura violação do Regulamento Geral sobre a Proteção de Dados (RGPD), equivalente europeu da LGPD brasileira.
Starlink registra imagens inéditas da Starship durante voo espacial
A SpaceX divulgou um novo vídeo mostrando a nave Starship em pleno voo espacial durante o 13º teste do foguete, realizado em 24 de julho. As imagens foram captadas por um dos novos satélites Starlink V3, que acompanharam a trajetória do veículo após serem liberados durante a missão.
Segundo a empresa, seis dos satélites lançados levavam câmeras para registrar o desempenho do escudo térmico do estágio superior da Starship. O material também revelou detalhes do voo da nave, incluindo o funcionamento de parte de seus motores e dos sistemas de controle de atitude durante a missão.
NASA admite que trajes lunares seriam um perigo para astronautas em Marte
O traje espacial mais avançado já desenvolvido pela NASA não serve para Marte. É o que concluiu uma equipe de engenheiros da agência e da indústria em apresentação no 55º International Conference on Environmental Systems (ICES).
O traje em questão é o Exploration Extravehicular Mobility Unit (xEMU), desenvolvido para as missões Artemis na Lua. Com 170 kg, é uma maravilha da engenharia moderna: resiste a grandes diferenciais de pressão, permite ampla mobilidade e é modular.
Mas na gravidade de Marte, que é 3/8 da terrestre, ainda pesaria 64 kg extras para o astronauta que o vestisse. Na Lua, onde a gravidade é 1/6 da terrestre, o mesmo traje equivale a apenas 28 kg.
Veja outras informações na matéria completa.
Calendário Astronômico de agosto traz eclipses e chuva de meteoros
Agosto chega repleto de atrações para quem gosta de observar o céu. Ao longo do mês, dois eclipses – um solar e outro lunar – estão entre os destaques, assim como o pico da chuva de meteoros Perseidas. E esses são apenas alguns dos fenômenos astronômicos que vêm por aí. Confira clicando aqui!
Especial do YouTube
Todo sábado, o Olhar Digital leva ao ar no YouTube um especial para se aprofundar em um assunto da Ciência ou da Tecnologia.
Desta vez, falamos de busca por vida fora da Terra – que entra numa nova fase. No vídeo a seguir, mostramos como a NASA pretende aumentar as chances de encontrar sinais de vida no Universo com duas das missões mais ambiciosas da história: o telescópio Nancy Grace Roman, que será lançado em breve, e o futuro Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), projetado para procurar bioassinaturas em planetas semelhantes à Terra.
Para explicar como esses observatórios podem transformar a astrobiologia, conversamos com exclusividade com Raíssa Estrela, pesquisadora do Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) da NASA e integrante da equipe do Habitable Worlds Observatory.
Ao longo da reportagem, ela detalha os desafios de detectar vida fora da Terra, as tecnologias que estão sendo desenvolvidas e por que o HWO pode representar um marco na história da exploração espacial.
Bruno Capozzi é jornalista, mestre em Ciências Sociais e editor executivo do OD.

articles.title: Cybersecurity And IT Support For Productive, Protected Workdays - Tech Guide
articles.text:
The Importance of Cybersecurity in Modern Work Environments
In today’s digital-centric business landscape, cybersecurity is no longer a luxury but a necessity. Organizations of all sizes face an increasing risk of cyber threats that can disrupt operations, compromise sensitive data, and cause significant financial losses. According to a recent report, cybercrime damages are expected to reach $10.5 trillion annually by 2025, up from $3 trillion in 2015, highlighting the exponential growth of this threat. This staggering figure reflects the urgency for businesses to strengthen their defenses against cyberattacks.
The consequences of inadequate cybersecurity are severe. Data breaches can lead to loss of customer trust, legal penalties, and irreparable damage to a company’s reputation. Furthermore, cyberattacks often result in operational downtime, which directly impacts productivity and revenue. In fact, the average cost of a data breach globally reached $4.35 million in 2022, emphasizing the financial stakes involved in protecting digital assets.
For businesses to maintain productive and protected workdays, safeguarding IT infrastructure against evolving cyber risks is critical. This involves not only implementing robust cybersecurity measures but also ensuring that IT support is readily available to address issues promptly and effectively. Proactive management of IT systems helps prevent downtime and data breaches, enhancing overall business continuity and resilience.
Integrating Cybersecurity and IT Support for Optimal Performance
A seamless integration of cybersecurity protocols with comprehensive IT support services is essential for sustaining business productivity. Cybersecurity tools such as firewalls, intrusion detection systems, and endpoint protection software serve as the first line of defense. However, without expert IT support to monitor, update, and troubleshoot these technologies, organizations remain vulnerable.
Many companies choose to discuss with Bryley Systems to leverage specialized knowledge and tailored cybersecurity strategies. These partnerships enable businesses to stay ahead of threats by adopting the latest security frameworks and best practices. Moreover, a dedicated IT support team can swiftly respond to incidents, minimizing the impact of any security breach or technical glitch.
Effective IT support goes beyond reactive problem solving; it includes ongoing system maintenance, vulnerability assessments, and compliance management. For example, ensuring that software patches and security updates are applied promptly can close exploitable gaps before attackers can take advantage. IT support teams also help enforce cybersecurity policies, such as strong password management and access controls, which are vital for protecting sensitive information.
The Role of IT Support in Enhancing Cybersecurity Posture
IT support teams play a pivotal role in maintaining a secure and efficient technological environment. They conduct regular system audits, apply critical patches, and ensure that all devices comply with security policies. According to a study, 60% of small businesses that experience a cyberattack go out of business within six months, underscoring the importance of ongoing IT support. This statistic highlights how devastating cyber incidents can be without proper IT defense and response.
Outsourcing technology supported by ChaceTech offers businesses access to experienced professionals who can manage complex IT infrastructures while implementing strong cybersecurity measures. This approach not only reduces the risk of cyber incidents but also alleviates the burden on internal staff, allowing them to focus on core business functions. External IT support providers often bring expertise in the latest cybersecurity technologies and threat intelligence, which smaller or resource-constrained companies might lack.
In addition, IT support teams assist with disaster recovery planning and execution. In the event of a cyberattack or system failure, having a tested backup and recovery plan can mean the difference between a brief interruption and prolonged downtime. Regular backups and data recovery drills ensure that businesses can quickly restore operations and minimize losses.
Best Practices for Cybersecurity and IT Support Collaboration
To maximize the benefits of cybersecurity and IT support, organizations should adhere to several best practices:
– Regular Training and Awareness: Employees are often the weakest link in cybersecurity. Regular training ensures staff recognize phishing attempts and understand security protocols. In fact, 91% of successful cyberattacks begin with a phishing email, making employee vigilance crucial.
– Comprehensive Incident Response Plans: Having a well-defined plan allows quick and coordinated action in the event of a cyberattack. This includes clear roles, communication strategies, and mitigation steps to reduce damage.
– Continuous Monitoring and Updates: Cyber threats evolve rapidly. Constant system monitoring and timely updates keep defenses strong. Employing tools like Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) can provide real-time threat detection and response.
– Data Backup and Recovery Solutions: Reliable backups ensure that data can be restored quickly after an incident, minimizing downtime. Ideally, backups should be stored securely offsite or in the cloud to protect against ransomware attacks.
These practices, combined with expert IT support, create a resilient security posture that supports uninterrupted productivity. Collaboration between cybersecurity specialists and IT support teams ensures that preventive and corrective measures are aligned, reducing vulnerabilities.
Leveraging Technology to Support Remote and Hybrid Work
The rise of remote and hybrid work models has introduced new cybersecurity challenges. Employees accessing corporate networks from various locations and devices increase the attack surface for cybercriminals. As a result, organizations need to implement secure remote access solutions such as virtual private networks (VPNs), multi-factor authentication (MFA), and endpoint security.
According to Gartner, by 2024, 70% of organizations will have adopted a hybrid work model, necessitating robust IT support to manage and secure diverse work environments. This shift demands flexible, scalable cybersecurity strategies that accommodate remote access without compromising security.
Businesses that can ensure their remote workforce remains productive and protected through continuous monitoring, security updates, and rapid technical assistance. Securing remote endpoints, enforcing strong authentication methods, and educating employees about safe remote work practices are vital components of this approach.
Moreover, IT support extends beyond security to include ensuring that remote employees have reliable access to necessary applications and data. Prompt resolution of technical issues reduces downtime and frustration, helping maintain high levels of productivity even outside the traditional office setting.
The Economic Impact of Cybersecurity and IT Support Investments
Investing in cybersecurity and IT support is not merely a cost center but a strategic business decision that can yield significant returns. According to a report by Accenture, companies that implement mature cybersecurity practices can reduce the cost of cybercrime by up to 72%. This demonstrates that proactive security and IT management can save organizations millions by preventing breaches and minimizing recovery expenses.
Furthermore, a secure IT environment contributes to customer confidence and competitive advantage. Clients and partners increasingly demand assurance that their data is protected, making cybersecurity a key factor in business reputation and growth. Organizations with strong cybersecurity and IT support frameworks are better positioned to comply with regulatory requirements, avoiding fines and legal repercussions.
Conclusion
Cybersecurity and IT support are inseparable components of a productive and secure workplace. As cyber threats become more sophisticated, organizations must prioritize both preventive security measures and responsive support services. Partnering with experienced providers and adhering to best practices ensures that businesses can operate smoothly, protect their data, and maintain customer trust.
By investing in a robust cybersecurity framework coupled with reliable IT support, companies can confidently navigate the complexities of today’s digital world while fostering a productive and protected work environment. This dual approach not only safeguards critical assets but also empowers employees to work efficiently without fear of disruption or compromise. In an era where cyber risks continue to escalate, the integration of cybersecurity and IT support remains a cornerstone of sustainable business success.

Avec leur surcouche One UI, les appareils Samsung sont sans aucun doute parmi les smartphones et tablettes Android les mieux lotis du côté des fonctionnalités. Cependant, parfois cette générosité peut se payer du côté de la batterie, sollicitée presque en permanence. Heureusement, il est assez aisé de désactiver des éléments pas nécessairement indispensables pour grapiller quelques pourcentages de batterie chaque jour. La plupart des astuces ci-dessous ne feront pas une différence majeure seules, mais en en cumulant plusieurs vous devriez commencer à voir la différence.
Démarrons par ce qui est probablement la fonctionnalité la plus gourmande de ce guide : l'affichage Always On Display (ou AOD). Utile pour les personnes qui veulent toujours avoir un œil sur l'heure ou sur leurs notifications, cette fonctionnalité qui laisse l'écran toujours allumé consomme certes moins que l'affichage complet normal, mais demeure un gros consommateur de batterie. Plusieurs options s'offrent ici à vous : désactiver totalement la fonctionnalité ou bien la régler pour, par exemple, ne l'afficher que lorsque vous appuyez sur votre écran.
Pour cela, direction : Paramètres > Écran de verrouillage et AOD > Always on Display (décochez pour désactiver ou appuyez sur le texte pour paramétrer la fonctionnalité avec l'entrée "Quand afficher").
Désactiver la fonctionnalité "Lever pour activer"
Dans la même veine que l'astuce précédente, où tapoter sur l'écran ou presser le bouton d'alimentation de son smartphone pour voir l'heure et ses notifications suffit, passons à la désactivation d'une fonctionnalité pour soulager deux capteurs qui n'ont pas besoin d'être en veille permanente, à savoir l'accéléromètre et le gyroscope. Utiles dans quelques situations, lorsqu'il est question de se repérer avec une application GPS notamment, ils sont aussi utilisés via la fonctionnalité "Lever pour activer". Cette dernière, comme son nom l'indique, allume l'écran dès que le terminal sent qu'il est levé via ces capteurs.
Pour désactiver cette feature qui oblige les deux capteurs à être alimentés en permanence, c'est simple : Paramètres > Fonctions avancées > Mouvements et gestes > Décochez Lever pour activer.
Limiter les autorisations de Bien-être numérique
Au sein de One UI, Samsung propose la fonctionnalité Bien-être numérique. Celle-ci surveille votre utilisation de votre appareil (temps d'écran, temps par application, etc.) afin de vous faire un bilan hebdomadaire et de vous fixer des objectifs et des minuteurs pour réduire votre consommation numérique. Un objectif louable, qui a cependant tendance à consommer un peu de batterie durant cette surveillance. Si vous pensez ne pas avoir besoin de Bien-être numérique, la solution pour désactiver cette fonctionnalité est de lui retirer les autorisations d'accès à vos données.
Pour ce faire : Paramètres > Bien-être numérique et contrôles parentaux > les trois petits points en haut à droite > Paramètres > Accès aux données d'utilisation > Paramètres > Décochez
Limiter la fréquence d'affichage de certaines applications
Pour cette astuce, il n'est pas vraiment question de désactiver une fonctionnalité, mais plutôt d'imposer une limite. Aujourd'hui, tous les smartphones proposent une fréquence d'affichage de 120 Hz ou plus. Sauf que bien des applications n'ont pas besoin d'aller au-delà des classiques et moins gourmands 60 Hz pour correctement afficher leur contenu. Malgré l'option "Adaptative" qui permet de jongler entre les fréquences en fonction des besoins, certaines applications utilisent trop souvent les 120 Hz, au détriment de la batterie. C'est par exemple le cas de YouTube, où les 120 Hz peuvent être utiles pour lire une vidéo, mais moins pour naviguer dans l'interface. Il est heureusement possible d'imposer une limite manuelle dans les trtréfondse One UI.
Comme déjà expliqué dans un précédent article (que vous pouvez aussi appliquer pour économiser de la batterie ) à propos des puces WiFi et Bluetooth qui consomment de la batterie en scannant en permanence leurs alentours même quand cela n'est pas forcément utile, les smartphones de chez Samsung scannent toujours autour d'eux pour accélérer l'éventuelle connexion à un accessoire (montre, écouteurs...). Sauf que s'il est question de gagner une poignée de secondes de temps à autre, cela se fait au prix de l'autonomie.
Pour désactiver cette fonctionnalité qui ne vous fera presque pas perdre de temps au moment de connecter vos appareils favoris : Paramètres > Connexions > Plus de paramètres de connexion > Décochez Recherche d'appareils à proximité.

articles.title: CXMT Reportedly Plans Second Fab in Beijing to Boost DRAM Output
articles.text:
Monday, August 3rd 2026
	
		
	
	
	
CXMT Reportedly Plans Second Fab in Beijing to Boost DRAM Output
Chinese memory maker CXMT is planning a second DRAM fab in Beijing amid high demand for its memory products. According to Reuters, the Chinese memory giant is considering building this second fab and is already in talks to secure funding for the project. As CXMT aims to boost its manufacturing output, measured in DRAM wafers per month (WPM), the company needs to secure new funding and is reportedly backed by the local government to increase production. While the project details are currently unknown, building a modern DRAM fab can cost over $10 billion, meaning CXMT will likely require significant funds to get started.
Currently, CXMT operates two 12-inch fabs, one in Hefei and one in Beijing, with each fab having an output of about 100,000 WPM. This means the current output capacity is around 200,000 wafers per month, with plans to triple that number to an astonishing 600,000 WPM when the Shanghai and Hefei plants are completed and fully operational. We have already reported that CXMT will end the year 2026 with about 350,000 WPM of DRAM output, just behind Micron's 375,000 DRAM WPM output.Although building a modern semiconductor plant takes years, CXMT is leading the industry in the speed of construction. Cleanrooms, where actual DRAM is manufactured away from any debris, are being built by CXMT in just 12 months, while the rest of the industry takes roughly two years. This is a significant speedup compared to the rest of the industry, as the entire supply chain is struggling to meet the massive demand driven by the AI data center buildout. CXMT's added capacity is likely to have a positive impact on the overall supply chain, but it will mostly be consumed by Chinese hyperscalers and AI labs for domestic demand.

articles.title: HashiCorp Ships Public Beta of Vault Kubernetes Key Management
articles.text:
HashiCorp has released the public beta of Vault Kubernetes key management, which lets Kubernetes clusters use Vault Enterprise as their KMS provider for encryption at rest.
Announced on the 10th of July, the release ships a KMS v2-compatible plugin called vault-kube-kms. It allows the Kubernetes API server to offload envelope encryption to Vault, protecting Kubernetes Secrets and other API resources stored in etcd, and moving the keys that guard that data outside the cluster.
The issue is not whether Kubernetes can encrypt data at rest; it can, but where the keys behind that encryption live. Writing on the HashiCorp blog, Rich DuBose and Steve Almy argue that if the same environment that stores sensitive data also controls the keys used to protect it, "the trust boundary remains too narrow". That leaves platform teams answering awkward questions about where key encryption keys are stored, who can reach them, how they are rotated, and how their usage is audited.
The plugin keeps the standard envelope encryption split. Kubernetes still generates and uses data encryption keys (DEKs) to encrypt sensitive resource data before it is written to etcd, preserving the throughput the API server expects. The DEK seed is protected by key encryption keys (KEKs) held in Vault, where the transit secrets engine performs the cryptographic operations. The encrypted data and the encrypted DEK are stored in etcd together. Without a reachable, correctly configured Vault, that data cannot be decrypted.
That split of duties is the practical benefit for regulated teams: Kubernetes handles high-volume encrypt and decrypt calls, while Vault owns key lifecycle, rotation, policy enforcement, and audit. HashiCorp's documentation lists centralised key management and RBAC, rotation workflows that retain the ability to decrypt existing data, and visibility into key usage, latency, and errors through Vault audit logs and plugin metrics. No application code changes are required.
HashiCorp points to enterprise Kubernetes platforms such as Red Hat OpenShift, multi-cluster production estates, regulated environments requiring separation of duties, and zero trust programmes as the main deployment scenarios. The company frames key management as increasingly a machine identity problem: applications, containers, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure automation, and AI agents all need continuous access to sensitive resources without human intervention, which puts more weight on an independently protected root of trust.
The capability is not entirely new territory. Managed platforms have offered similar integrations for some time, including Azure Key Vault KMS for AKS, and community projects such as vault-kubernetes-kms have filled the gap for self-managed clusters. HashiCorp Discuss threads going back several years show platform teams repeatedly asking for an official Vault-backed Kubernetes KMS provider. The difference here is a vendor-supported path for teams already standardised on Vault Enterprise, with tested support across recent Kubernetes minor releases.
There are constraints worth noting for anyone evaluating the beta. It is Vault Enterprise only, and deployment requires the ability to modify the Kubernetes EncryptionConfig and the kube-apiserver manifest, which rules out most fully managed control planes. Teams also need to think through Vault availability, since the KMS provider sits on the path for decrypting cluster data.
HashiCorp describes the beta as a first step toward centralised key management for Kubernetes encryption at scale, and is inviting platform engineering and security teams to evaluate it and provide feedback.

articles.title: Lo nuevo de Gemini en Google Docs acaba con lo más aburrido de los documentos colaborativos
articles.text:
Los documentos colaborativos son una gran herramienta para cuando varios integrantes de un equipo tienen que trabajar sobre un mismo proyecto. En especial, cuando la tarea se completa a distancia o los participantes no interactúan personalmente a diario. Pero también es una realidad que las correcciones grupales pueden volverse bastante aburridas, pues alguien siempre encuentra algo más que modificar, añadir o quitar, haciendo que el proceso se vuelva eterno. Por suerte, lo nuevo de Gemini en Google Docs promete acabar con el tedio.
En los últimos días, Google Docs introdujo nuevas funciones impulsadas por Gemini en los comentarios de los documentos colaborativos. La inteligencia artificial ahora tiene un rol más preponderante al momento de lidiar con el feedback que ofrecen los integrantes del equipo. Esto permite que el flujo de trabajo sea más ágil y no se pierda el tiempo en nimiedades.
Gemini no se limita a resumir los comentarios de tus compañeros de equipo, ni tampoco a identificar los problemas o correcciones que se estén marcando. La IA de Google también tiene la capacidad de modificar tus documentos para implementar los cambios que se están recomendando o solicitando a través de los comentarios colaborativos.
Pero mucho ojo: esto no significa que Gemini va a modificar el contenido de tus archivos en Google Docs sin que estés al tanto de ello. Ni tampoco, sin contar con tu autorización explícita. Todas las acciones que proponga la inteligencia artificial tendrán que ser revisadas y aprobadas por ti, lo cual simplifica bastante la tarea.
Gemini mejora los documentos colaborativos en Google Docs
Gracias a la integración con Google Docs, ahora puedes pedirle a Gemini que sintetice hilos de comentarios completos o que se enfoque en los cambios que propone un usuario en particular. Asimismo, puedes indicarle que agregue tus propios comentarios. Esto significa que, en lugar de escribir el feedback tú mismo, la inteligencia artificial puede hacerlo siguiendo tus indicaciones.
Respecto de la edición de documentos colaborativos en Google Docs, tienes la opción de pedirle a Gemini que sugiera modificaciones basadas en los cambios propuestos por alguno de tus compañeros. Por ejemplo: “Reescribe el párrafo 5 siguiendo las correcciones de X, pero manteniendo el estilo y respetando las estadísticas incluidas en el mismo”. La IA será capaz de seguir tu instrucción y presentarte las modificaciones propuestas, que, si las aceptas, se podrán añadir con un clic.
Pero ni siquiera tendrás que ser tan específico al pedirle a Gemini que optimice tus documentos colaborativos en Google Docs. Puedes solicitarle que encuentre todos los problemas aún no resueltos y que presente un plan de edición para darles solución a todos. Luego, solo tendrás que aprobar los cambios (si están a la altura de lo que necesitas), y listo. Sin dudas, una posibilidad muy interesante y que promete optimizar los documentos colaborativos, que muchas veces pierden el hilo conductor en un mar de comentarios, sugerencias y correcciones.

articles.title: Xbox prices are increasing by up to €200 or £170
articles.text:
When Microsoft announced its latest round of Xbox price bumps in June, it only gave US pricing. Now we know the pricing increases for the EU and UK, and they’re dramatic. Depending on the model, Xbox prices are increasing by up to €200 or £170. The 1TB Xbox Series X with a disc drive is going up by over 30 percent from £499.99 / €599.99 to £669.99 / €799.99. The 512GB Xbox Series S is getting a price increase of over 43 percent, jumping from £299.99 / €349.99 to £429.99 / €499.99.
Xbox prices are increasing by up to €200 or £170
Microsoft’s struggling console continues to see unprecedented price bumps.
While other consoles have received price bumps as RAM and storage prices skyrocket due to demand from the AI industry, none have been quite as dramatic as Microsoft’s. This is the third round of price increases since May of 2025, with the highest-end model now costing $300 more than its launch price of $499.99 in 2020. The 2TB model is also being retired in the face of the storage crunch. Here’s the full list of price changes:
512GB Xbox Series S was €349.99 / £299.99, now €499.99 / £429.99
1TB Xbox Series S was €399.99 / £349.99, now €599.99 / £519.99
1TB Xbox Series X Digital was €549.99 / £449.99, now €749.99 / £619.99
1TB Xbox Series X Disc was €599.99 / £499.99, now €799.99 / £669.99

articles.title: SpaceXAI says it will remove all 69 of its unpermitted turbine power generators, but expects process to take a year — trailer-mounted generators to be replaced by 1.2GW power plant
articles.text:
SpaceXAI says it will remove all 69 of its unpermitted turbine power generators, but expects process to take a year — trailer-mounted generators to be replaced by 1.2GW power plant
Why would it take a year to remove mobile turbines?
Elon Musk’s Colossus data centers that sit near the border between Tennessee and Mississippi will finally be removed starting this month. According to the company, the 69 temporary mobile turbines, which have been the subject of a lawsuit that claims they have been causing pollution, are going to be completely removed by July 2027, meaning it will take the company 12 months to withdraw the trailer-mounted generators from its premises. This may sound confusing, as they’re “portable” generators, after all, but it seems that SpaceXAI is removing them in phases as its 1.2GW power plant slowly comes online.
SpaceXAI achieved one of the fastest data center deployments ever after it set up 100,000 Nvidia H200 GPUs in 19 days — something that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said usually takes four years or more. Musk achieved this by bringing in his own power instead of waiting to get connected to the grid, which was considered a novel idea at that time. Today, a few data center operators, like OpenAI, are following Musk’s footsteps and deploying their own turbines to power their servers without relying on other providers.
But even though the idea feels innovative, the community surrounding the Colossus 1 and Colossus 2 data centers has been complaining about the pollution that these mobile turbines bring. They say that these turbines didn’t have the required permits to operate, although the company argued that the mobile and temporary nature of these units exempted them. The EPA said earlier this year that these units aren’t exempt from permits, but SpaceXAI continued to operate them anyway. It has even got to the point that the NAACP filed a case over these unpermitted turbines, although the DOJ weighed in, saying that removing them would put national security at risk as Colossus 2 “supports mission-critical operations.”
Despite that, it seems that SpaceXAI has finally settled into an agreement with the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality. It’s if the 1.2GW power plant replacing these mobile turbines is the same one that Musk is importing from overseas, but the important part is that it’s approved under a Clean Air Act permit. Aside from that, the company also said that it’s equipping all its mobile turbines with “advanced emission control technologies,” which should reduce the environmental impact of its power sources.

articles.title: Malgré la crise et la concurrence, Tesla vient de franchir un record historique
articles.text:
Pour une marque, passer un seuil dans sa production est toujours un moment de célébration. C’est le résultat d’années de travail acharnées qui ont payé. Tesla entre ainsi dans le club des constructeurs ayant produit 10 millions de véhicules. Si cette étape est lointaine pour les firmes historiques, c’est un cap symbolique pour la jeune marque américaine. Il suffit de revenir un peu en arrière pour voir à quel point les choses se sont accélérées.
Une accélération fulgurante qui force le respect
Le millionième véhicule a en effet été produit douze ans après les débuts. Et six ans plus tard, la dix millionième voiture est sortie des chaînes de production de l’usine californienne de Fremont. Certains clameront que BYD a franchi la barre de 10 millions de modèles en 2024. C’est factuellement vrai, mais il s’agit de « véhicules à énergies nouvelles » comme aime souvent le rappeler le constructeur chinois.
La mise au point cash face au géant BYD
Autrement dit, il englobe des voitures électriques, mais aussi des voitures hybrides rechargeables, ce qui aide forcément à gonfler les chiffres de production. Flatteur donc pour Tesla, d’autant plus que la partie était très loin d’être gagnée. Car si la marque a réellement décollé en 2017 avec l’arrivée de la Model 3 puis en 2019 avec le déploiement du Model Y, la suite n’a pas été aussi rose que prévu.
La descente aux enfers évitée de justesse ?
Les ventes ont fortement baissé à partir de 2024 pour deux raisons principales : la première concerne le rapprochement d’Elon Musk aux côtés de Donald Trump qui n’a pas plu à une grande partie de la clientèle. Le second concerne directement la gamme Tesla qui vieillit à vue d’œil. Figurez-vous que les Model S, X, Y et 3 en sont toujours à leur première génération ! Un cas unique dans l’industrie automobile atténué par des mises à jour régulières. Si l’extérieur a timidement évolué sur les Model S et X, l’intérieur a tout de même subi de beaux changements pour rattacher les wagons.
Le tournant risqué : entre échec du Cybertruck et pari du tout-autonome
Mais face à une concurrence accrue, cela commence à être de plus en plus juste pour garder la couronne. Le polémique Cybertruck, qui devait exploser tous les scores, est finalement un pétard mouillé. La marque californienne préfère dorénavant se focaliser sur les véhicules autonomes avec son Robotaxi sur base de Model Y et son Cybercab, qui commence tout juste à prendre la route.
20 millions de véhicules, le défi impossible ?
Si Tesla reprend un peu des couleurs en Europe, le chemin vers les 20 millions de véhicules risque d’être extrêmement difficile. Pour rendre cela possible, il faudrait urgemment de nouveaux modèles au sein de la gamme. Le Model YL, qui est simplement un Model Y rallongé, ne pourra marquer l’essai seul. Une compacte de taille européenne aurait de quoi faire un carton absolu, mais aucune information n’a encore été confirmée à ce sujet.

articles.title: Infomaniak va entrer en Bourse : voici ce que cela change pour vos données personnelles
articles.text:
Infomaniak va rejoindre la Bourse suisse via un rachat inversé de Perrot Duval Holding, une opération pensée pour lever des fonds sans céder le contrôle de son capital.
L'hébergeur genevois avait déjà transféré la majorité de ses droits de vote à sa fondation en mai. Cette entrée en bourse prolonge cette même logique de protection contre toute prise de contrôle extérieure.
Un rachat inversé plutôt qu'une introduction classique
Techniquement, Infomaniak ne s'introduit pas en bourse au sens traditionnel du terme. L'opération passe par un rachat inversé (reverse takeover). Concrètement, il s'agit d'un montage dans lequel une société non cotée rejoint une société déjà cotée pour profiter de sa place en bourse plutôt que de mener sa propre introduction. Perrot Duval Holding, coté en Suisse depuis 1905 et aujourd'hui présent sur le SIX Swiss Exchange, doit au préalable céder ses activités industrielles. Cette opération est elle aussi soumise à l'accord de son assemblée générale. Cette même assemblée devra ensuite valider la transaction avec Infomaniak le 24 septembre prochain. Si elle est approuvée, la structure cotée qui en résultera sera renommée Infomaniak SA.
Ce chemin évite les délais d'une introduction en bourse classique, tout en gardant la même transparence réglementaire : un prospectus, attendu autour du 2 septembre 2026, et la surveillance des autorités boursières suisses. Infomaniak explique que cette opération lui permettra de lever des financements. L'hébergeur va en effet investir dans de nouveaux centres de données en Suisse destinés à répondre à la demande européenne croissante de services cloud souverains. Infomaniak va aussi étendre ses services cloud et collaboratifs, le tout, en poursuivant la création d'emplois à Genève et Zurich. L'entreprise construit sa croissance depuis 1994 sans capital extérieur, en réinvestissant l'intégralité de ses bénéfices depuis 2017. Elle revendique plus de 300 employés en Suisse et environ 300 000 clients payants, pour un chiffre d'affaires de 54,2 millions de francs suisses en 2025 contre 47,6 millions un an plus tôt.

La fondation garde la majorité des voix, quoi qu'il arrive en bourse
Cette opération ne change rien à la gouvernance mise en place par Infomaniak en mai dernier. Nous rapportions alors que Boris Siegenthaler avait transféré la majorité des droits de vote de l'entreprise à la Fondation Infomaniak, une structure d'utilité publique placée sous la surveillance des autorités cantonales genevoises. Cette même fondation détiendra les actions de catégorie A de la future Infomaniak SA. Il s'agit de titres non cotés et non cessibles, et surtout, qui concentrent la majorité des droits de vote. Seules les actions de catégorie B seront échangées en bourse, sans donner accès au contrôle de l'entreprise.
Un investisseur pourra donc acheter une part de la valeur économique d'Infomaniak, jamais de son pouvoir de décision. Aucun rachat ne sera possible sans l'accord de la fondation, elle-même liée par une charte des participations signée devant notaire. Cette charte fixe neuf principes fondateurs, dont l'indépendance, la souveraineté numérique et la protection de la vie privée. Pour les utilisateurs, l'entreprise ne prévoit aucun changement : mêmes services, mêmes tarifs, mêmes contrats, mêmes équipes.
