articles.title: Architecting AI Systems for the Messy Reality of Enterprises: Why Agentic Compute is the Missing Layer
articles.text:
Transcript
Arun Joseph: My talk today is going to focus entirely on enterprises. There will be different definitions of agents. You might have heard about Cursors, Lovables, and autonomous agents that run for hours, but I'm going to ground it in the context of enterprises. That's why I call it agents for the rest of us in enterprises. Building anything greenfield is easy. If you want to, in enterprises, you already have the cars, you already have the trucks, you need to lift it up and then fly. This is the aura that AI actually brings in.
My name is Arun Joseph. I was here talking about our journey in my previous role as head of AI engineering for Deutsche Telekom. There was a program that we did, which we envisioned in 2023. We were one of the first agentic platforms to go live, potentially, as I know, in Europe or elsewhere, and that too in a large enterprise like Deutsche Telekom. I was leading that program. It was entirely built open source. It's called LMOS. It stands for Language Models Operating System. It's now moved under Eclipse Foundation and still running in Deutsche Telekom across multiple countries. Ever since, I have moved on. Last year's talk was so successful that I decided to quit my job and then start my own entrepreneurial journey, leaving a cushy job. This is what InfoQ talks can do to you. Right now, we are entirely focused on building multi-agent systems. One of the companies, a lot of things are under stealth. It's called Masaic. M-A-S stands for multi-agent systems by its nature. My previous background has always been building platforms across the world, including Europe, U.S., Canada. Distributed systems has been my mainstay in large enterprises.
Context
I'm going to talk a little bit about what we do as a company. We focus on operational intelligence systems. We build large-scale operational intelligence systems for critical infrastructure and large enterprises. We could say, a better Palantir is what we are actually looking at, with an open core. Essentially, all of this comes from the learning that we had building agentic systems. There is a need for a new class of systems, which we refer to as system of outcomes. We already know about systems of record, which is Salesforces and databases of the world. Then we have the data OS layers, which is the Palantirs and the dashboards of the world. You need a new class of systems, which sits on top of these systems, which focuses on outcomes, whether it's heavy machinery downtime, or running a city better, or for thriving of the industry in operations matters. Part of several foundations. I will focus entirely on enterprises.
Let's start with the myth bust on what actually works in enterprises, at least from the journey that I had. Then we will try to define an agent, because there are so many definitions. I wouldn't be theoretical, I would try to frame my mental model of an agent that we use even today, and the enterprise challenges. There are two magic bullets, which are going to solve everything in enterprises, which I'm going to give to you. Then we are going to level up the agent's journey. I'll show you some demos.
Myth Bust - Agents that Work
Agents that work in enterprises. Let's start with two categories of agents that work. A little bit of background on LMOS. It went live in 2023. This has since moved out of Deutsche Telekom. Some of these numbers are public numbers. I won't cite the numbers around agent handover, but it has been incredibly massive in terms of what we could do. There are three outcomes that was done. One was the business outcomes, which is obvious, without which there is no technical platform. It was an industry first, and it was tested against some of the best in the industry, vendor products, and it still outshone them. The best part was it showed how you can leverage existing investments and teams within an enterprise to build agentic systems right from scratch when agents wasn't a thing at all. The kind of systems that we do, so one category of systems that work is the chat modes and automation systems, which is where most of the enterprises are, but we are actually going into operational intelligence systems.
I'll show you a glimpse of a couple of agents, what we refer to as agents. The core of our operational intelligence platforms is also multi-agent systems. I'll use the heavy machinery operations as an example to talk about the agents that we refer to as agents in the level 2 of agents. One of our core products is called Atlas, but I won't go into the details. Let's take a heavy machinery operations company, it could be Hitachi, John Deere, SENNEBOGEN, whatever it is. Essentially you want to reduce the downtime of machines, because the downtime of machines is costly. How do you ingest all the data that you have about the machine? For example, you have IoT data, telemetry data, SOPs, all the incidents, the frontline intelligence, which is where most of the intelligence lies. How do you ingest all of that into a system, let's call it the magical system, so that a service operations manager can ask, we have seen a spike in error codes of this one in Midwest, what can we do about it?
Do you know anything about it? This is the system experience of what it would be. It needs to drill down, crunching numbers. It needs to be accurate, and come up with suggestions like this. "Look at it. It looks like 73% of the use cases are around air filter management issues, and here are the classification of those issues." Maybe there are better ways that we can deal with it. Decisions, it's actually a decisioning system. At this point, the large operational intelligence scheme can decide what to happen, what can be done with it. Then, it should actually go into the next step, which is, let's do the automation of this, potentially. What can we do about this? Maybe when this error happens, this is the SOP that needs to be followed, which has human in the loop, then raise these tickets, but also send this telemetry data to some other systems.
Which results in a dynamic construction of an SOP, which is not just textual, it is a mix of agentic actions, plus documents, plus a process that needs to be followed with human in the loop, which is sent to humans for approval and for testing. This is a second class of agentic systems, which is not really the chatbots and the typical enterprise agentic systems.
My talk is going to focus on this class of systems, and in the end, it's going to show, here are the ways in which you can reduce your machine downtime. Look at this. These two parts have been failing consistently in this region for the last one month. Here are the next actions that you can take. JP-100, or seal kit across these warehouses, stock it up. Maybe there is a need in the next couple of months. How do you build such a system? This is what we are going to talk about. Here, while building that system, as you would see, essentially, when you ask such a question, what actually happens underneath this? It's going to spin out multiple research tasks, and each of these tasks are ephemeral agents. This is not like agents somebody has created with X and Y framework. This will not work, because how many agents will you create?
You need an ability to create ephemeral agents. Then it actually runs and says, find the most frequent mode, so the multi-agent execution in parallel. Then in the top, you will have a multi-agent synthesis, which arrives at the outcomes. This is a true agentic system, as we envision it to be, which is what we are building. We're going to talk about these two classes of agentic systems.
What is an Agent?
What is an agent? Let's start with the level 1 agent, which is mostly used in enterprises for chatbots, automations. This is the definition that I use for an agent as a programming paradigm. You have programming paradigms like functional programming, object-oriented programming. My definition of agent here is not from the perspective of what an agent is from a theoretical sense, but from a programming paradigm sense. What is a program? A program has input. It does some transformation or computation, then it produces the output. I would define agent as a program, the level 1 agent as a program, which at least has one characteristic. It expands the breadth of inputs that it can take, and it expands the adaptiveness of the computation. It is still abstract. Let me show you two examples. This is, for example, from one of the agent frameworks that we built from LMOS.
This is a screenshot. "Hey, find me the best hotel in the location with the warmest weather between three cities, and book it for me." Imagine if you are a traditional enterprise with a booking system, for example, that you built. articles.title: Doom now "runs" in Microsoft Paint thanks to a wildly inventive clipboard trick
articles.text:
WTF?! It's long been established that Doom can be made to run on pretty much anything with a screen, but this ability goes beyond mere devices. The latest example of the classic FPS's legendary portability involves Microsoft Paint essentially being used as a monitor that displays the original shareware version of the game – and the project was developed by Microsoft Azure CTO Mark Russinovich.
Called DoomPaint, Russinovich's creation doesn't literally execute Doom inside Microsoft's drawing app. Instead, ViZDoom, a ZDoom-based platform designed primarily for AI research, runs the engine and renders it headlessly. It loads the genuine shareware DOOM1.WAD for the first episode, while maps not included with that release use the BSD-licensed Freedoom WADs.
Every rendered frame is placed on the Windows clipboard as a bitmap and pasted onto the Paint canvas as a genuine document edit. A low-level keyboard hook captures the usual movement, strafing, shooting, and door-opening controls while Paint remains the active window, preventing the keystrokes from affecting the drawing app.
Making the process work smoothly required more than endlessly hammering Ctrl+V. Russinovich writes that an early version repeatedly overwrote the clipboard, sometimes replacing frame data before Paint had finished reading it. DoomPaint instead publishes a single OLE data object and updates the image bytes it supplies. Paint's reads also signal when the next frame can be made available, avoiding the race condition.
Performance depends on the PC and selected resolution, which can range from Doom's native 320 x 200 up to 640 x 480. The engine runs on its own thread at Doom's native 35Hz tic rate, meaning the displayed frame rate is capped at 35 fps and may be lower depending on how quickly the machine can make Paint process and composite the pasted images.
The setup brings some entertaining side effects. Because every frame is a real Paint edit, Ctrl+Z can move backward through them, while choosing File > Save produces a PNG screenshot. The project also includes the original Episode One music, converted from Doom's MUS format to MIDI on the fly, alongside sound effects supplied by the engine.
"Paint renders the game but does not compute it. Paint computes nothing. Paint has never computed anything. That's the joke," Russinovich explains.
DoomPaint is available on GitHub under an MIT license. Running its batch file creates a Python virtual environment and installs the required dependencies. ViZDoom boots directly into a map, so there are no title screens, demos, or in-game menus, and performance can sometimes fall to what Russinovich calls "spreadsheet-tier."

articles.title: Half of adults admit they would publish work created mainly by AI and not say so — despite believing other people should do just that
articles.text:
Half of adults admit they would publish work created mainly by AI and not say so — despite believing other people should do just that
AI has trust issues
- Over two-thirds (69%) of people believe AI generated material can be presented as their own work if they provided the prompt and approved the final version
- Meanwhile, 54% believe AI-based work should be clearly marked
- 7,200 adults were surveyed, located across the US, the European Union, the UK, and Latin America
A growing disparity in how AI generated content, tasks, and tools are assigned ownership and expectations on accurately marking their origins is emerging, according to a new survey by Use.AI.
Furthermore, the findings indicate an emerging dichotomy between human-claimed authorship of an AI work and clear labeling of the work as AI.
Different attitudes based on settings for the AI work have also been identified, such as private emails and school or professional reports.
The chicken or the prompt?
The developing adoption of AI appears to be introducing new attitudes to acceptable creativity, with the emerging model of what is described as “authorship by direction,” where the AI is trusted to create a first draft, which is then revised and claimed by a human.
The statistics shared by Use.AI – a tool that aggregates AI models into a single interface – highlight how AI is being used more extensively, with a human-originating prompt leading to drafts and versions from the machine, followed by editing from the human.
While the AI has contributed, only a human name appears on the finished product, which raises questions of ownership and authorship.
“AI is separating the production of work from the ownership of it. People are increasingly prepared to direct the process, approve the result and take the credit, but there is still no shared standard for when AI’s role should be visible to everyone else,” says Use.AI’s Managing Director, Ihor Herasymov.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
With 69% of those surveyed considering AI-generated work their own if they produced the prompt, 46% claiming they would keep AI involvement with their work under wraps, and 54% feeling AI use should be disclosed, we’re some way from agreement on AI use across creative tasks.
Authorship vs. editorship
Herasymov’s observations point to a constantly evolving set of standards around the creation and use of AI-generated materials. Interestingly, this is happening against a backdrop of growing unease over the use of AI in creative tasks.
The implications of claiming ownership of automated work generated upon instructions to an LLM trained on as much human writing, art, music, and cinema as possible are considerable, and go way beyond questions of ethics. Copyright is just one element, and the most obvious, but we’re also moving into a landscape where inputting a prompt on employer-owned hardware takes authorship away from the person at the keyboard.
Ultimately, the task of prompting and revising means anyone using AI in this way stops being the author, and becomes the editor – and that is before the true ownership of the output is determined.

articles.title: ‘Mother Mary’, crítica: Anne Hathaway encarna la estrella pop definitiva y falla al hacerlo
articles.text:
Mother Mary evita ser un drama musical convencional. Y lo hace, planteando desde sus primeras escenas que su protagonista (una misteriosa Anne Hathaway) es mucho más que una estrella. En realidad, el director y guionista David Lowery enfoca la idea desde la posibilidad de que esta cantante seductora sea algo más que una mujer. Por lo que el guion, intenta mostrar que la protagonista, una combinación de Madonna y Sia, es tanto una artista talentosa como algo más tenebroso.
De hecho, las mejores partes de Mother Mary ocurren cuando el director plantea directamente una posible doble lectura para su misterioso personaje. A mitad de camino entre una diva y una especie de sacerdotisa, el personaje de Hathaway es inquietante. Pero además, un símbolo para ideas más complejas. Para eso, analiza la posibilidad de que la celebridad en la actualidad sea una especie de devoción cercana a un culto. Uno, además, que consume a los fanáticos desde una experiencia casi religiosa.
Por lo que Mother Mary muestra la cultura de la celebridad desde una perspectiva casi ritual. Un escenario en que el éxito deja de ser un objetivo profesional para convertirse en una fuerza capaz de alterar la percepción de la realidad. Para eso, en lugar de explicar de inmediato quién es Mother Mary, la cinta permite que el personaje exista como una presencia que domina cada espacio antes incluso de pronunciar una palabra. Esa decisión cambia por completo la experiencia del espectador. No importa tanto la biografía de la cantante como el efecto que produce sobre el mundo. Un concepto que la película intentará explorar varias veces, no siempre con buenos resultados.
Una mirada a la fama desde un ángulo perverso en ‘Mother Mary’
David Lowery utiliza esa idea para plantear una pregunta incómoda. ¿Qué ocurre cuando una sociedad deposita toda su necesidad de creer en una persona de carne y hueso? La propuesta funciona porque jamás presenta la admiración como un fenómeno superficial. El director sugiere que existe un impulso casi primitivo detrás de la fascinación por los ídolos contemporáneos. Las multitudes no solo buscan entretenimiento. También necesitan encontrar figuras capaces de representar deseos, frustraciones y esperanzas imposibles de explicar con palabras.
La trama de Mother Mary convierte esa dependencia emocional en un elemento inquietante. Como si el escenario escondiera un altar donde los seguidores entregan voluntariamente parte de su identidad. Ese planteamiento conecta con una constante dentro de la filmografía de Lowery, interesado desde hace años en personajes que viven atrapados entre lo cotidiano. Todo en medio de un eterno escape de cualquier explicación racional.
Pero en la cinta, el misterio no se relaciona con fantasmas evidentes ni criaturas sobrenaturales. Más bien, lo hace desde la ambigüedad de plantear que el fenómeno inexplicable no sea Mary, sino quienes necesitan contemplarla. Esa inversión del punto de vista convierte la película en un análisis sobre la necesidad humana de fabricar mitologías modernas. Cada actuación pública adquiere el peso de un acontecimiento irrepetible y cada gesto cotidiano parece esconder un significado secreto. Como si el poder en la actualidad tuviera relación directa con la capacidad de cautivar a las masas.
Un personaje ambiguo para una actriz polifacética
La propia construcción de Mother Mary alimenta esa sensación de incertidumbre permanente. El guion evita definirla mediante explicaciones convencionales y prefiere convertirla en una figura cuya identidad cambia dependiendo de quién la observe. Para algunos representa una artista extraordinaria; para otros, una inspiración casi espiritual. También existe la impresión de que detrás de su imagen pública permanece escondida una dimensión imposible de comprender del todo.
Lowery juega constantemente con esa ambigüedad sin transformarla en un rompecabezas destinado a resolverse. El argumento de Mother Mary parece mucho más interesado en explorar la experiencia de convivir con el enigma que en proporcionar una respuesta definitiva. Esa decisión provoca que cada escena funcione como una pieza abierta, susceptible de múltiples interpretaciones. Incluso cuando Mary permanece inmóvil frente a una multitud, la puesta en escena transmite una tensión difícil de describir.
No obstante esta cuidadosa ambición, no siempre se sostiene más allá de la puesta en escena o de las interacciones de Mary con otros personajes. En realidad, en lo que Mother Mary falla estrepitosamente es en que no llega a profundizar en ninguno de sus temas centrales. Antes que eso, todos parecen insinuaciones incompletas de algo mayor que no llega a revelarse jamás. En especial, cuando la película cambia de temperatura al incorporar plenamente a Sam Anselm (Michaela Coel). Esta última, una diseñadora cuya historia compartida con Mary introduce un conflicto mucho más íntimo que cualquier espectáculo multitudinario.
Dos historias sin relación entre sí
No obstante, al carecer de explicaciones retrospectivas, el vínculo entre ambas parece artificial y hasta forzado. No hay una historia o una forma de entender completamente la rivalidad y el miedo entre ambas. Mucho más, porque el guion evita brindar a alguna, el papel tradicional de heroína o antagonista. Las dos parecen compartir responsabilidades dentro de una historia donde el éxito ha terminado deformando aquello que originalmente las unía. Pero una premisa tan interesante de nuevo queda incompleta porque el guion no llega a explorar del todo en su complejidad.
Un punto bajo que afecta la forma en que la película cuenta su historia cuando se interesa en el confuso vínculo entre ambas mujeres. Eso sin explicar en realidad qué ocurre entre ellas (¿rivalidad? ¿enfrentamiento? ¿celos?) o introducir un elemento real de misterio. Luego de casi dos horas de hacer más densa la atmósfera, la incapacidad de la trama por realmente mostrar algo misterioso, decepciona. Pero peor aún, deja claro que la trama carece de objetivo real al contar su historia.
Para su anticlimático final, Mother Mary desperdicia toda su sofisticada puesta en escena, en solo insinuaciones de algo más complejo y raro que nunca ocurren. Un elemento confuso que evita que la película logre unir todas sus piezas o, en cualquier caso, enlazar ideas acerca de los temas que ya planteó. Una falla que no supera nunca y que vuelve la experiencia de la película una tediosa y pretenciosa visión sobre la fama que no llega a ninguna parte.

articles.title: Helsinki-based Aiforia secures €20 million EIB financing to advance AI-powered cancer diagnostics | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Aiforia, a Helsinki-based life-science company providing deep learning AI solutions for pathology, has secured €20 million in venture debt financing from the European Investment Bank (EIB).
Supported under the European Commission’s InvestEU programme, the financing will accelerate Aiforia’s product development and boost its commercial operations. The financing is divided into three tranches, with a first tranche of €5 million. Drawing each tranche requires meeting the revenue and other interim targets set out in the financing agreement. Aiforia and the EIB have also agreed on a synthetic warrant arrangement, which does not cause immediate share dilution for Aiforia’s existing shareholders.
“We are pleased that the negotiations have led to the signing of a binding financing agreement. The EIB venture debt financing strengthens Aiforia’s financial position and supports the implementation of our strategy. With this financing, we can accelerate product development, expand our commercial operations internationally, and advance our goal of improving patient care through AI-powered image analysis solutions,” said Jukka Tapaninen, CEO of Aiforia.
Founded in 2013 as a spin-off from the University of Helsinki, Aiforia is a publicly traded company operating internationally with thousands of platform users across the globe. The company states that it delivers software solutions that elevate diagnostic capabilities in image analysis, enabling medical discoveries. It equips pathologists and scientists in preclinical and clinical labs with deep learning AI software for translating images into discoveries, decisions, and diagnoses.
Aiforia claims that over 1 million images have been analysed and thousands of AI models have already been developed on the Aiforia platform for research use, and several diagnostic solutions have been deployed.
Selected Aiforia® Clinical AI models and the Aiforia® Clinical Suite Viewer are CE-IVD marked for diagnostic use in EU and EEA countries.
Aiforia is a publicly traded company operating internationally with thousands of platform users across the globe. Headquartered in Helsinki, the company also operates subsidiaries in the United States and France, and maintains a network of local representatives across Europe and North America. Aiforia’s team includes AI and software developers, pathologists, medical scientists, and a commercial team.
“Our continent is working to remain competitive, and we need to support the companies that make that possible. From healthcare to digital life sciences, Europe must have the best technologies developed in-house to protect and care for its citizens. The solutions developed by Aiforia strengthen Europe’s competitiveness, while giving an innovative EU company the opportunity to succeed on the global stage,” said EIB Vice-President Karl Nehammer.
The funding will support the further development of the company’s AI-powered platform, designed to support pathologists in digital tissue analysis (digital pathology), notably for the detection of tumours, as well as to boost its commercial operations.

articles.title: RTX 5060 Ti survives car crash after being bent in half — short PCB saves the day, single memory chip resolder restore full performance
articles.text:
RTX 5060 Ti survives car crash after being bent in half — short PCB saves the day, single memory chip resolder restore full performance
Because it had a rather short PCB.
Buying a new GPU is always a joyous occasion, but the celebration was cut short for an unfortunate customer in China. Right after buying an AX Gaming RTX 5060 Ti, they got into a serious car crash that ended up totaling the car — and the card along with it. Fortunately, the driver was safe, and somehow the GPU survived, too, with no major electronic damage. Despite being bent in half, the card ended up only requiring minor repair work and was brought back to life quickly by Brother Zhang.
Visually, the card didn't look salvageable, and midrange GPUs like these often don't make for feasible repair jobs either because of the high labor cost. The backplate and cooler were completely destroyed, so Brother Zhang separated them from the actual PCB. Luckily, this variant of the 5060 Ti used a very short PCB that just barely touched the point of curvature, so the internals were mostly fine.
The technician checked all the power rails for a short circuit but saw no abnormal resistance, which confirmed the core and memory weren't dead. He then proceeded to quickly test the GPU with its bare PCB, and it booted successfully. Brother Zhang devised a makeshift cooler that consisted of the bent fin stack straightened back to the best of his abilities, and two 120mm fans strapped on top via zip ties. This seemed enough to keep the card cool.
However, as soon as he tried to install drivers, the PC would black screen and hard crash, showing consistent signs of instability. At this point, Brother Zhang reopened the card and inspected the PCB. He inspected the flex point and decided to resolder the memory module closest to the edge of the board since it experienced the most torque. A simple removal and reapplication fixed the issue, and the card was detected correctly as a 5060 Ti with the full 8GB of VRAM.
Brother Zhang rechecked for any short circuits to ensure no solder bridges were created during the BGA work before moving on to benchmarking. In Furmark, the temps peaked and stabilized at 64°C with no visual artifacts. He then ran a full 3DMark loop to test the PCIe 5.0 x8 link speeds — the card passed with a high 98.9% stability score. It drew around 92% of its maximum power limit during the run, with core temps peaking at around 67°C. This 5060 Ti was officially a survivor.

Lexar Lists 32 GB DDR5-7200 Memory With Chinese DRAM at $592
Lexar has introduced a new THOR RGB DDR5 Gen 2 32 GB memory kit, consisting of two 16 GB DDR5 modules, specifically for the Chinese market. The kit features DDR5 memory running at 7,200 MT/s, with the actual DDR5 modules produced by an unidentified Chinese DRAM manufacturer, likely CXMT. The latest THOR RGB 32 GB kit offers memory with 38-48-48-86 CAS latency timings at 1.40 V and supports Intel's XMP 3.0 and AMD EXPO profiles to achieve maximum frequency and overclocking potential. While the exact overclocking range of these modules is unknown, 
Lexar has not explicitly disclosed which Chinese DRAM maker is used for this DDR5 kit, but it is assumed that CXMT DRAM is housed under the sandblasted aluminium heat spreaders. The company tested a variety of ASUS and MSI motherboards on both AMD and Intel platforms, even mentioning a 32 GB kit with 7,600 MT/s speeds, as opposed to this newly listed 7,200 MT/s kit. It is likely that more motherboards and vendors will be compatible without issues, but only those mentioned in the list below were tested. articles.title: HP’s HyperX Omen 15 isn’t quite the budget-friendly gaming laptop its predecessor was
articles.text:
The HP HyperX Omen 15, which I first saw at CES, replaces the HP Victus 15, a longtime bestselling budget gaming laptop. The Victus cost just $800, or less when on sale, and was a good entry point to decent laptop gaming.
HP’s HyperX Omen 15 isn’t quite the budget-friendly gaming laptop its predecessor was
But it’s decent enough for 1080p gaming in our RAMageddon world.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
The Omen 15 has nice little upgrades over the Victus. Its RTX 5050 Laptop GPU can play 2026’s latest games, albeit on low-ish settings. But it’s also got a brighter 16:10 aspect ratio display with higher refresh rate, and a 1080p webcam to make it a little better for non-gaming stuff.
I’d call it a working-class gaming laptop, but thanks to RAMageddon, the Omen 15 starts at $1,200 — a far cry from the $800 that made its predecessor so appealing. But laptop prices are way up across the board, and if you want current-gen gaming hardware, this is about as cheap as you’re going to find it.
The Good
- Affordable-ish gaming performance in a decent to solid package
- Fine for 1080p / 1200p gaming and light content creation
- 165Hz refresh rate on a fairly bright screen
- Upgradeable DDR5 RAM and NVMe SSD (with two slots for each)
The Bad
- Not as affordable the HP Victus 15 it replaces
- Only one of the USB ports is USB-C — and not even Thunderbolt
- No face or fingerprint unlocking
- Keyboard, trackpad, and speakers range from okay to bad
Component report card
- Screen: C
- Webcam: C
- Keyboard: C
- Trackpad: D
- Port selection: C
- Speakers: C
- Number of ugly stickers to remove: 3
Our HyperX Omen 15 review unit is a $1,199 configuration sold through Walmart with an eight-core Intel Core 5 210H “Raptor Lake” chip, RTX 5050 discreet GPU, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, and 512GB SSD. There are pricier Omen 15 configs out there with RTX 5070 GPUs and OLED screens, but that’s like spending Acura money on a Honda Civic. On the lower end, HP still has a Victus 15 config with the RTX 5050 for $900, but it has 8GB of RAM — that’s not really tenable, especially for playing the latest games.
The good news is that the Omen 15 with an RTX 5050 is pretty serviceable for playing games at its 1920 x 1200 native resolution. Last-gen games like Control can get a smooth 70 to 80fps on High preset while using DLSS. Cyberpunk 2077 can run on the Ultra preset (no ray tracing) with DLSS set to Quality and get 60 to 70fps— sometimes dipping down to 40 while driving with lots of stuff onscreen. Standard frame generation boosts it to 95 to 105fps, and 70s to low 80s in a car. Multi Frame Gen, which you don’t get on last-gen GPUs, can push that ever further if you don’t mind more “fake frames.”
Newer games are a more Medium to Low affair. For example, Helldivers 2 runs comfortably at just above 60fps on its Medium preset with DLSS set to Quality — though it dips into the 40s when the bug guts hit the fan. But Battlefield 6 was lower, down in the 50fps range while running Medium preset with DLSS cranked to Performance. I also tested Halo: Campaign Evolved, which defaulted to its Very Low preset, where it looked like a potato. On Low settings, with DLSS set to Medium, it mustered between 50 to 60fps, but with frequent drops into the 40s with lots of enemies onscreen.
While playing all these games, the fans kicked up to a decent volume, but they weren’t obnoxiously loud, and the chassis stayed reasonably cool. The hottest point, a small spot under the chassis, rose to 113 degrees Fahrenheit / 45 Celsius. But the main areas that normally make contact with your hands or lap didn’t get too warm — pretty good thermals for a somewhat compact gaming laptop.
So the RTX 5050 GPU and its 8GB of VRAM can get by with the latest graphically intense games, so long as you’re not expecting a visual powerhouse. But what about living with the rest of the laptop?
Much of the Omen 15’s price has gone to its specs. That means there are some rough edges showing in the usual areas. The trackpad has a responsive mechanical click, but if you pick up the laptop by either of its front corners the chassis flexes and causes an accidental click. This is common in mostly plastic laptops, but still annoying.
The keyboard has decent enough tactility when typing. But even though I know gamers love a number pad, it makes this 15-inch laptop feel cramped. I don’t enjoy typing on it like I have other HP laptops. The speakers? A little muddy-sounding — especially for music. And the ports? It has HDMI 2.1 and gigabit ethernet, which is great, but only one USB-C to go with its two USB-A ports. And all of them are a modest 10Gbps — not particularly speedy compared to USB4 or Thunderbolt 4. Gaming laptops are supposed to have ports aplenty, but this is just ports apassable.
Aside from its gaming performance, the Omen 15’s other strength is its screen. The 1920 x 1200 IPS panel isn’t particularly special, but at 400 nits it’s decently bright and it has nice contrast and colors. It’s good for games, and fine for productivity work and light content creation. I did a bit of Lightroom Classic editing on the Omen 15, and my 50-megapixel RAW files were workable at a modest clip. (It helped that I was editing a batch of under 50 images, and not, like, 2,000.) The bigger problem with trying to do creative things was the Omen’s paltry 512GB of storage. It fills up quickly when games like Battlefield 6 take up 142GB. There’s a second M.2 slot for another drive, just as there’s a second RAM slot, which is great for future upgrades — but boy will that cost you right now. You can hold out for RAM and SSD prices to come back down to Earth, but if that takes as long as it’s expected to, the Omen 15 might feel pretty outdated by then.
The Omen was also fine for my everyday work: Chrome tabs, four virtual desktops, Signal, Slack, music streaming, etc. While the 1080p webcam is a little grainy and slightly low in saturation, it looks fine on video calls. The main barrier to getting work done on the Omen 15 is that its battery never lasted me more than five and a half hours. That’s far from the worst for gaming laptops, but keep that chunky power adapter with its barrel plug nearby.
The HyperX Omen 15 is a decent gaming laptop. It’s just not the value the Victus 15 used to be. But neither is anything else. Absent a really good sale, you’re going to pay over $1,000 for anything with the RTX 5050, and usually a lot more. But buying into even the bottom rung of the 50-series gets you all of Nvidia’s latest features, like Multi Frame Gen and whatever DLSS 5 eventually shapes up to be. Last-gen 40-series or AMD GPUs aren’t bad options, but Multi Frame Gen can help keep frame rates playable for longer.
It’s still worth looking for those sales, though. HP, Best Buy, and Walmart often have deals on most of HP’s product line. Even now, there’s an Omen 16 with an RTX 5060 GPU and slightly larger (but dimmer) screen for just $100 more than the Omen 15.
RAMageddon makes buying a new gaming laptop daunting. If you need to buy now and you don’t want to go open-box or secondhand, you just have to come to terms with the fact that you’re going to be paying higher prices than equivalent models from a year or two ago — even in the “entry level.” Considering the circumstances, the Omen 15 is an okay value at $1,200 for getting into laptop gaming.

- CPU: Intel Core 5 210H (Raptor Lake, 8 cores)
- GPU: Nvidia GeForce RTX 5050
- RAM: 16GB DDR5 (two SODIMM slots, user-accessible)
- Storage: 512GB NVMe M.2 (two slots, user-accessible)
- Webcam: 1080p
- Connectivity: Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.3

- Weight: 5 pounds / 2.27kg

articles.title: N-able Says Attackers Take Over N-central Servers After Initial Fix Proves Incomplete
articles.text:
N-able said attackers exploited an authentication bypass in N-central to gain remote administrative access and reach the customer systems managed through those servers.
Its first fix was incomplete. CVE-2026-18577 affects N-central builds prior to 2026.3.1.7. N-able shipped build 2026.3.1.7 on August 2 as the first unaffected version.
N-central is the remote monitoring and management platform managed service providers and IT teams use to administer customer endpoints.
After compromising an N-central server, the attackers used Take Control to reach managed endpoints and registered Cloudflare tunnels as services on the devices. The tunnels connect outbound to Cloudflare's edge, so they need no inbound firewall rule or open listening port.
Running them as services lets them survive a reboot. N-able said the tunnels preserved access after the route through the N-central server was revoked. Nothing in the disclosure suggests Cloudflare was compromised; the attackers abused its tunneling service.
Every N-central customer should be on 2026.3.1.7. Upgrading to 2026.3, N-able's initial instruction, is no longer sufficient. N-able's hotfix notice says hosted NCOD instances will be upgraded automatically on a schedule communicated directly to partners; self-hosted servers must be upgraded by the customer.
Customers that find evidence of compromise must also hunt for and remove malicious tunnel services from managed endpoints, because upgrading N-central does not remove persistence installed on another machine.
N-able began investigating on July 31 after an unusual volume of licensing errors from on-premises customers. It found that an attacker had remotely gained administrative access to servers running 2026.1 and earlier. N-able said it identified and contacted a limited number of affected customers but did not provide a figure.
The first flaw, CVE-2026-18556, is titled "unauthenticated administrative account takeover" in N-able's own CVE record and classified as an authentication bypass through an alternate path or channel, or CWE-288.
N-able assigned both CVEs and scored each 8.2 on CVSS 4.0. Neither record identifies the vulnerable endpoint or request sequence, and N-able has published no code-level root-cause detail.
CVE-2026-18556 covers releases through 2026.1. N-able said it fixed that path in 2026.2, but later found an alternative way to exploit the same vulnerability that the earlier fix did not block. That finding became CVE-2026-18577 and expanded the affected range to builds before 2026.3.1.7.
Finland's national cyber security centre said in an August 2 advisory that all versions available before the emergency hotfix were vulnerable.
The Hacker News has reached out to N-able for clarification on the incident's scope and incomplete patch. This story will be updated with any response.
N-able has now published six IP addresses seen in the attacks:
- 173[.]249[.]252[.]200
- 87[.]249[.]138[.]34
- 37[.]19[.]210[.]32
- 37[.]153[.]90[.]88
- 92[.]118[.]112[.]181
- 68[.]235[.]46[.]214
Huntress later identified the four addresses from N-able's initial list as Mullvad or NordVPN exit nodes. Huntress advised correlating any matches with N-central UI, network, and endpoint logs.
N-able also told customers to look for svchost.exe in users' Documents folders, a service named Cloudflared, or traffic from the published IP addresses. It advised customers who find any of these indicators to contact support and engage their security teams.
Huntress, in a rapid response published August 3, initially said it had seen exploitation at one organisation in its customer base and published three attacker domains: mousears.synology[.]me, wagoosh.direct.quickconnect[.]to, and who-ripped-one.direct.quickconnect[.]to.
In an email to The Hacker News, Huntress clarified that the activity involved a self-hosted N-central instance within one partner account. The attackers accessed nine organisations under that account, reaching one endpoint in each.
Based on the evidence available so far, Huntress said the post-compromise activity was limited to enumerating running processes on the endpoints before the attackers disconnected. The company is continuing to review the activity for other indicators of compromise and attacker tradecraft.
Huntress said it did not observe the Cloudflare installation activity that N-able described in its original notification to affected customers.
For signs of unauthorized Take Control activity, Huntress recommended checking ui_access_control.log and correlating it with C:\ProgramData\GetSupportService_N-Central\Logs\BASupSrvc_*.log.gz on Windows endpoints. Those logs also appear during legitimate Take Control use, so their presence alone is not proof of compromise.
It also advised investigating sessions tied to apparent N-able support identities, such as mspsupport@n-able.com.
N-able has not disclosed the number or identities of affected customers, how many downstream devices were reached, when exploitation began, who is behind it, or whether any data was taken.

articles.title: Nigeria’s Treepz launches CMS T&M to launch new TMO Rides service - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nigerian mobility startup Treepz has partnered CMS Transport Management (CMS T&M), one of Lagos’ longest-standing transport operators, to launch a new service known as TMO Rides, designed to simplify the daily commute by introducing seamless cashless payments for passengers across its bus network.
Founded in 2019 and known as Plentywaka until its September 2021 rebrand, Treepz operates a digital platform allowing passengers to book daily rides along fixed routes. It also serves as an aggregator for bus travel companies across dozens of cities in Nigeria, allowing transport operators to replace manual servicing and ticketing with digitalised offerings and services.
Treepz has announced a strategic partnership with CMS T&M to modernise public transportation through digital technology to ensure cashless, transparent and more efficient commuting for passengers across CMS – Ajah routes. The partnership brings together Treepz’s transportation technology and CMS T&M’s decades of experience moving passengers.
By integrating Treepz’s digital mobility platforms into CMS T&M’s operations, passengers will enjoy a faster, safer and completely cashless payment experience, while the transport operators gain access to real-time operational insights, digital ticketing and improved revenue management.
The launch of TMO Rides will give passengers access to TMO Cards for seamless transport. Beyond introducing digital fare payments, the initiative reflects CMS T&M’s broader commitment to modernise public transportation through innovation, operational efficiency and improved customer experience.
“For nearly six decades, our focus has remained the same, which is moving people safely and efficiently. As the transportation needs of Lagos continue to evolve, we must evolve with them. TMO Rides is about making everyday commuting easier by giving our passengers a faster, more convenient way to pay while improving the overall travel experience. This launch represents another important step in our commitment to building a smarter, more accessible transport system for everyone,” said Andrew Akhigbe, managing director of CMS T&M.

articles.title: IT Consulting And Managed IT For Everyday Operational Gains - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Unlocking Operational Efficiency Through IT Consulting
In today’s fast-paced digital environment, businesses must leverage technology not only to survive but to thrive. IT consulting and managed IT services have become essential components for companies seeking to enhance everyday operational gains. By partnering with skilled IT consultants and managed service providers, organizations can optimize their technology investments, streamline workflows, and ultimately boost productivity.
The value of IT consulting lies in its ability to provide tailored strategies that align with a company’s unique operational needs. For instance, AdRem Systems’ consulting expertise offers businesses in various industries the guidance necessary to modernize their infrastructure, improve cybersecurity measures, and implement scalable solutions. This consulting expertise helps organizations identify inefficiencies and implement best practices that translate into measurable improvements across daily operations.
IT consulting goes beyond simple technology recommendations; it involves a deep dive into the business processes, challenges, and goals. Consultants analyze current systems and workflows, identify bottlenecks, and recommend technologies that integrate seamlessly with existing operations. This comprehensive approach ensures that technology investments are not just upgrades but strategic enablers of growth and efficiency.
Recent research indicates that companies engaging in IT consulting experience up to a 35% increase in operational efficiency within the first year of implementation. This significant improvement stems from adopting best practices, automating repetitive tasks, and optimizing IT infrastructure to support everyday activities effectively.
How Managed IT Services Drive Consistent Business Performance
Managed IT services complement consulting by delivering ongoing support and maintenance, ensuring that IT systems run smoothly and securely. This proactive approach minimizes downtime and allows businesses to focus on core activities without the constant worry of technical disruptions. According to a recent study, companies that adopt managed IT services experience a 50% reduction in IT-related downtime, which directly correlates with increased operational output and revenue growth.
The role of IT experts at All In IT highlights how specialized IT teams can provide continuous monitoring, rapid issue resolution, and expert advice tailored to the evolving technological landscape. Their hands-on management of IT infrastructure enables businesses to stay agile and responsive, adapting quickly to market changes without compromising operational stability.
Managed IT services typically include network monitoring, data backup and recovery, cybersecurity, and help desk support. This comprehensive coverage ensures that potential issues are detected and resolved before they impact business operations. Additionally, managed services providers often leverage advanced tools such as artificial intelligence and machine learning to predict failures and optimize system performance proactively.
A survey by CompTIA revealed that 83% of businesses that use managed IT services reported improved security and operational stability, underscoring the vital role these services play in everyday business functions. By outsourcing IT management, companies can access specialized expertise and technology that might otherwise be cost-prohibitive to maintain internally.
Integrating IT Consulting and Managed Services for Maximum Impact
The synergy between IT consulting and managed services offers a comprehensive approach to operational optimization. Consulting lays the foundation by assessing current IT environments and recommending improvements, while managed services execute and maintain these enhancements effectively. This combination ensures that technology investments yield ongoing benefits rather than one-off gains.
For example, a mid-sized manufacturing firm that invested in IT consulting for process automation saw a 40% improvement in production efficiency after implementing the recommended solutions. When paired with managed services, the firm maintained system reliability and security, preventing costly disruptions that could have negated those gains.
This integrated approach allows businesses to remain proactive rather than reactive. IT consultants identify long-term strategic goals and design systems that support scalability and flexibility. Managed IT teams then handle daily operations, ensuring those systems perform optimally and evolve with emerging needs. Together, they form a feedback loop of continuous improvement, where insights gained from managed services inform future consulting engagements.
Moreover, businesses benefit from enhanced disaster recovery and business continuity planning when combining these services. Consultants develop robust strategies to safeguard critical data and operations, while managed IT providers implement and test these plans regularly, ensuring minimal disruption during unforeseen events.
Real-World Benefits of IT Consulting and Managed IT
Businesses that engage in both IT consulting and managed IT often report improvements in several key operational areas:
- Enhanced Security Posture: Cyber threats are increasingly sophisticated, making robust security a necessity. IT consultants help design solid cybersecurity frameworks tailored to specific risks, and managed services provide ongoing protection and rapid response, reducing the risk of breaches. Notably, companies using managed security services reduce breach costs by 25% on average.
- Cost Efficiency: Outsourcing IT management reduces the need for in-house specialists and costly emergency fixes. Companies can predict IT expenditures more accurately through managed services, ensuring budget alignment with operational goals. According to a study by Deloitte, businesses can reduce overall IT costs by up to 30% when leveraging managed IT services alongside consulting.
- Improved Compliance: Regulatory compliance is critical in sectors such as healthcare and finance. IT consulting identifies compliance gaps and recommends necessary changes, while managed services maintain the necessary controls and documentation to meet regulatory standards continuously, reducing the risk of fines and reputational damage.
- Scalability and Flexibility: As businesses grow or pivot, their IT needs evolve. Consulting services plan for scalability by designing modular and adaptable systems, and managed IT providers adjust resources dynamically to support changing demands. This agility enables companies to seize new opportunities quickly without being hampered by outdated infrastructure.
- Increased Employee Productivity: Streamlined IT systems reduce downtime and provide employees with reliable tools, enhancing their efficiency. A report by Microsoft found that organizations leveraging managed IT services experienced a 20% increase in employee productivity due to reduced system issues and faster problem resolution.
Selecting the Right IT Partners for Everyday Gains
Choosing the right IT consulting and managed services partners is crucial for realizing the full potential of technology investments. Factors to consider include industry experience, service breadth, responsiveness, and proven success in delivering operational improvements. Engaging experts ensures access to deep knowledge and comprehensive support tailored to specific business challenges.
Separately, working with specialized managed IT providers guarantees continuous operational support and security. By partnering with distinct experts for consulting and management, businesses benefit from focused expertise in each domain.
Moreover, businesses that prioritize collaboration with their IT partners often outperform competitors. A recent survey found that 70% of companies with integrated IT consulting and managed services reported higher customer satisfaction and operational efficiency than those that did not.
When evaluating potential partners, organizations should also consider their technological compatibility, communication style, and ability to scale services as the business grows. A strong partnership is built on trust, transparency, and a shared commitment to continuous improvement.
Conclusion: Leveraging IT for Sustainable Operational Success
Incorporating IT consulting and managed IT services into everyday business operations is no longer optional-it’s a strategic imperative. These services empower organizations to modernize their IT infrastructure, safeguard critical data, reduce costs, and scale effectively. By engaging trusted IT experts and leveraging their insights and support, businesses can transform technology from a cost center into a powerful enabler of operational excellence.
Ultimately, the journey toward everyday operational gains through IT requires thoughtful planning, expert execution, and continuous improvement. With the right partners and a proactive approach, businesses can harness the full potential of IT to drive sustained growth and competitive advantage.
As technology continues to evolve rapidly, companies that invest in comprehensive IT consulting and managed services will be better positioned to adapt and thrive. The combination of strategic guidance and hands-on management ensures operational resilience and ongoing innovation, critical factors for success in today’s competitive landscape. By making IT a core component of their business strategy, organizations unlock new opportunities for efficiency, security, and growth that translate into tangible everyday gains.

articles.title: Disney+: lançamentos da semana (3 a 9 de agosto)
articles.text:
Toda semana, o Olhar Digital destaca as novidades do Disney+ no Brasil. Entre os dias 3 e 9 de agosto de 2026, o streaming recebe novas temporadas, séries inéditas, filmes e episódios de produções em andamento.
Nesta atualização, o Disney+ recebe a animação Star Wars: Visions Apresenta – A Nona Jedi e o filme Psycho Killer. O catálogo também ganha a terceira temporada de Os Feiticeiros Além de Waverly Place, a estreia da série Estilhaços, novos episódios de X-Men ’97 e Uma Loja Para Assassinos, além da temporada 14 de Futurama.
Lançamentos do Disney+ de 3 a 9 de agosto de 2026
Confira abaixo mais detalhes sobre os lançamentos da semana no Disney+ entre 3 e 9 de agosto de 2026:
Segunda-feira – 03/08
- Fúria — Temporada 1, episódio 4
  - Série | Original Hulu | Policial | Drama | Suspense | Ano de Produção: 2026 (EUA)
  - Da criadora Elizabeth Meriwether, Fúria acompanha a agente do FBI Alice Black (Emmy Rossum) na busca por uma misteriosa e calculista assassina em série. À medida que as duas seguem seus próprios caminhos rumo à justiça, a linha entre o bem e o mal se torna cada vez mais tênue.
- Futurama — Temporada 14
  - Série | Original Hulu | Animação | Aventura | Comédia | Ficção científica | Ano de Produção: 2026 (EUA)
  - Na 14ª temporada de Futurama, o futuro está prestes a ficar ainda mais estranho com uma avalanche de piratas espaciais, carne cultivada em laboratório, golpes de sedução e o surpreendente retorno do grande amor perdido do Dr. Zoidberg.
Quarta-feira – 05/08
- Star Wars: Visions Apresenta – A Nona Jedi
  - Série | Original Lucasfilm | Animação | Ação | Aventura | Ficção científica | Ano de Produção: 2026 (EUA e Japão)
  - Como parte da iniciativa Star Wars: Visions Apresenta, a série de oito episódios dá continuidade à história iniciada nos curtas Visions: A Nona Jedi e A Nona Jedi: Filha da Esperança. Lah Kara segue seu treinamento nos caminhos Jedi sob a orientação de Margrave Juro e embarca em uma jornada de autodescoberta ao lado de uma comunidade de aprendizes em uma missão para salvar seu pai.
- Psycho Killer: Em Busca do Assassino
  - Filme | 20th Century Studios | Policial | Drama | Terror | Suspense | Ano de Produção: 2026 (EUA e Alemanha)
  - Após o assassinato brutal de seu marido, uma oficial da patrulha rodoviária do Kansas embarca em uma caçada ao responsável pelo crime. Conforme a investigação avança, ela descobre que o culpado é um sádico serial killer e que a profundidade de sua depravação mental e seus planos sombrios são muito mais perturbadores do que poderia imaginar.
- Estilhaços — Temporada 1, episódios 1 e 2
  - Série | Original FX | Drama | Terror | Mistério | Suspense | Ano de Produção: 2026 (EUA)
  - Estilhaços, do FX, é a nova série dramática do produtor executivo Ryan Murphy, baseada no romance de Bret Easton Ellis. Ambientada na Los Angeles dos anos 1980, a produção acompanha um grupo de alunos do último ano de uma exclusiva escola preparatória enquanto enfrentam conflitos ligados à identidade, sexo, ciúmes e obsessão, além dos perigos que se escondem sob a superfície da adolescência norte-americana.
- Os Feiticeiros Além de Waverly Place — Temporada 3
  - Série | Original Disney+ | Comédia | Drama | Família | Fantasia | Ano de Produção: 2026 (EUA)
  - Na terceira temporada de Os Feiticeiros Além de Waverly Place, Billie, ainda abalada por ter perdido Alex no fim da segunda temporada, descobre que a única maneira de salvar sua mãe é reencontrar seu pai, desaparecido há muito tempo. Enquanto a família Russo se une em busca de Alex, Billie percebe que a união dos poderes da família é a única forma de derrotar o mal que os ameaça.
- R.J. Decker – Investigador Privado — Temporada 1
  - Série | ABC | Ação | Comédia | Policial | Drama | Mistério | Ano de Produção: 2026 (EUA)
  - Escrita por Rob Doherty e estrelada por Scott Speedman, a série acompanha R.J. Decker, um ex-fotógrafo de jornal e ex-presidiário que recomeça a vida como detetive particular no sul da Flórida. Ao lado de sua ex-esposa, que trabalha como jornalista, da atual esposa dela, uma detetive, e de uma misteriosa mulher de seu passado, ele resolve casos que vão do estranho ao bizarro enquanto tenta reconstruir a própria vida.
- 9-1-1 — Temporada 9, novos episódios
  - Série | ABC | Ação | Drama | Suspense | Ano de Produção: 2026 (EUA)
  - Criada por Ryan Murphy, Brad Falchuk e Tim Minear, 9-1-1 acompanha a rotina de profissionais da linha de frente, como policiais, bombeiros e operadores de emergência, que enfrentam situações extremas enquanto tentam equilibrar a pressão do trabalho com os desafios de suas vidas pessoais. Inspirada em histórias reais, a série mostra o cotidiano de socorristas diante de ocorrências imprevisíveis, intensas e emocionantes.

  - À beira do divórcio, Kang Tae Ju vê sua vida virar de cabeça para baixo quando sua esposa é sequestrada por criminosos impiedosos. Tornado o principal suspeito do crime, ele precisa fugir da polícia e dos sequestradores para tentar salvá-la antes que seja tarde demais.

articles.text:

| Technologies biométriques | Capteur d'empreinte digitale, Reconnaissance faciale simple |

| Module Photo arrière 2 | Ultra grand-angle, 50 Mpx, f/1,9 | 
| Module Photo arrière 3 | Zoom optique x3, 10 Mpx, f/2,4 | 
| Autonomie |  | 
| Capacité de la batterie | 5000 mAh | 
Avec le Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, Samsung pousse encore plus loin sa vision du smartphone pliant haut de gamme. Plus ambitieux que jamais, ce nouveau modèle entend surtout faire oublier une facture qui atteint elle aussi de nouveaux sommets.
Avec le Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, Samsung repense sa gamme de smartphones pliants. Le constructeur, présent sur ce marché depuis 2019, doit désormais composer avec des rivaux plus offensifs et l’arrivée très attendue d’Apple sur le segment à la rentrée 2026.
La réponse passe donc par une nouvelle hiérarchie : le format du Z Fold 7 devient Ultra, tandis qu’un Fold 8 au format passeport occupe l’échelon inférieur. Une logique censée rapprocher les séries Z et S, même si le changement de nom ressemble aussi à une habile façon de maquiller une hausse des prix.
Ce modèle est malgré tout l’évolution directe du Galaxy Z Fold 7, sorti l’été dernier. Samsung mise sur un boîtier encore aminci, une puce haut de gamme, une batterie en silicium-carbone, un écran interne renforcé et un volet photo amélioré. L’ensemble vise l’ultra-premium face aux Motorola Razr Fold et Honor Magic V6.
La facture suit ce positionnement : comptez 2199 € en version 12/256 Go, soit 100 € de plus que le Z Fold 7, qui avait déjà subi une augmentation de 100 €. Chez Samsung, l’Ultra désigne donc aussi le tarif — au moins, le message est-il clair.
Le Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 a soigné son summer body avec 215 g sur la balance, moins que les 224 g atteints par certaines versions du Honor Magic V6. Fermé, il mesure 158,4 x 72,8 x 8,9 mm ; ouvert, il passe à 158,4 x 143,2 x 4,1 mm, soit encore 0,1 mm de gagné. Il est aussi moins encombrant qu’un Galaxy S26 Ultra (163,6 x 78,1 mm). Malgré cette finesse rare pour un pliant, il ne paraît pas fragile, même si l’on resserre instinctivement la prise.
Son châssis en aluminium Armor associe légèreté et rigidité avec du verre Gorilla Glass Victus Ceramic 3 devant et du Victus 2 au dos. Les deux parties se rejoignent sans interstice une fois l’appareil refermé. La charnière paraît robuste et supporte les manipulations franches, mais sa fermeté peut compliquer un peu l’ouverture. Déplié, le terminal inspire confiance, sans toutefois donner envie de tester sa résistance aux chutes… On n'est pas des brutes !
À l’extérieur, le cover display couvre près de 86 % de la façade. Ses bordures contenues rapprochent l’usage de celui d’un smartphone haut de gamme classique, tandis qu’une caméra selfie prend place en haut dans un poinçon centré. Sur la tranche droite, très plate, les commandes restent faciles à atteindre. Le lecteur d’empreintes est par ailleurs intégré au bouton d’alimentation.
La reconnaissance faciale complète l’arsenal de sécurité, même si elle n’est pas aussi poussée que Face ID d’Apple. Samsung ajoute d’ailleurs un second module photo dans un poinçon situé sur la partie droite de l’écran interne. Ce dernier s’étale quant à lui sur plus de 90 % de la surface disponible. La pliure centrale se montre encore plus effacée au regard comme au toucher, grâce à une nouvelle charnière et la structure Flex Titanium.
Cette construction ajoute un plateau en titane rendu souple par des microperforations, puis une couche supérieure en alliage de titane. Elle a pour effet de limiter la marque du pli et empêcher qu’elle se creuse avec le temps. Le bloc photo rappelle celui des S26 mais dépasse d’environ 4 mm, rendant le smartphone instable sur une table, ouvert comme fermé. Une coque peut réduire ce mouvement, qui devient vite agaçant dès qu’on l’utilise à plat.
Côté connectivité, il prend en charge la 5G, le NFC, le wifi 7 et le Bluetooth 6. Les charges sans-fil et inversée sont également présentes. En revanche, il n’y a ni emplacement microSD, ni prise casque, ni compatibilité S Pen, officiellement pour gagner de la place et faute d’un usage suffisant. Enfin, la certification IP48 protège contre les petits éléments de plus de 1 mm ou un bref plongeon dans la piscine.
Pour aller plus loin :
Le Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra réunit deux dalles Amoled LTPO : un écran de 8 pouces (2504 x 2256 pixels, 422 ppp) à l’intérieur, et un autre de 6,5 pouces (2520 x 1080 pixels, 422 ppp) à l’extérieur. Leur fréquence s’ajuste de 1 à 120 Hz selon l’usage, permettant ainsi un affichage plus fluide et une économie d’énergie. L’Oled assure en prime des noirs parfaits, un contraste théoriquement infini et aucune rémanence perceptible.
Nos sondes ont relevé un pic de luminosité à 2880 cd/m² sur l’écran interne (0,95 cd/m² à son minimum), tandis que le cover display atteint une luminosité comprise entre 1,17 et 2876 cd/m². Tous deux restent donc exploitables en plein soleil comme dans une pièce mal éclairée. Par défaut, l’afficheur externe propose un delta E de 1,96 et une température des couleurs légèrement froide à 6704 K ; à l’intérieur, on obtient 2,15 et 6651 K. Certes, le mode Naturel améliore la fidélité des couleurs, à 1,49 et 1,68, mais réchauffe trop l’image autour des 6270 K (loin des 6500 K de référence).
Enfin, le nouvel écran Flex Titanium, évoqué précédemment, ne se contente pas d’atténuer la pliure centrale. Il bénéficie aussi d’un traitement anti-reflets. Nos tests l’ont d’ailleurs confirmé : l’afficheur interne présente une réflectance de seulement 23,45 % (il renvoie donc moins de 24 % de la lumière que refléterait notre miroir de référence). À l’extérieur, ce taux atteint environ 46 %, mais sans pour autant altérer le confort de lecture grâce à sa forte luminosité.
Le Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra s’appuie sur le Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 “for Galaxy”, gravé en 3 nm et épaulé par 12 Go de RAM. Cette version optimisée réunit deux cœurs Oryon V3 Phoenix L à 4,74 GHz, six cœurs Phoenix M et un GPU Adreno 840. La puissance ne manque donc pas, même pour ceux qui gardent une application ouverte “au cas où”, puis 15 autres.
Même s'il n'égale pas son aîné, le multitâche constitue son point fort. Malgré l’exécution simultanée de nombreux logiciels, l’appareil conserve une réactivité exemplaire et rejoint le podium de notre comparatif. Il devance notamment le Honor Magic V6, pourtant muni du même processeur, et exploite efficacement ses deux écrans pour enchaîner les usages sans ralentissement perceptible.
En jeu, le format ouvert, proche du 4:3, demande un temps d’adaptation, mais les résultats sont excellents : 125 images par seconde (i/s) en moyenne avec des pointes à 137 i/s. La fluidité tient bon dans nos scénarios exigeants. Le châssis peut néanmoins approcher 42 °C lors des tâches lourdes. Ce n’est pas excessif pour un appareil aussi fin, d’autant que l’on craignait la surchauffe, tant certains modèles dotés de la même puce ont déjà souffert de montées de fièvre handicapantes.
Contrairement au Z Fold 8 qui sacrifie le zoom optique, le Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra intègre un triple module photo composé d’un capteur principal de 200 Mpx (f/1,7), un ultra grand-angle de 50 Mpx (f/1,9) et un téléobjectif x3 de 10 Mpx (f/2,4). Un trio dont la firme sud-coréenne vante les talents de jour comme de nuit.
Dans de bonnes conditions lumineuses, le capteur principal du Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra offre une image détaillée et bien exposée, avec un piqué convaincant au centre, des teintes naturelles et une dynamique maîtrisée. Les bords manquent un peu de netteté, mais restent sans défauts majeurs. Les textures sont également un peu lissées, mais les couleurs moins saturées que son rival chinois.
La nuit, l'appareil livre des photos aux couleurs naturelles et contours bien définis, même si elles manquent de détails. Le centre reste net avec des inscriptions lisibles, mais les textures fines sont lissées et quelques artefacts colorés apparaissent. L’exposition est globalement bonne, bien que les ombres soient denses et les hautes lumières brûlées sur les surfaces réfléchissantes.
De jour, l’ultra grand-angle du Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra capture des clichés nets et détaillés au centre avec des textures bien restituées et une colorimétrie respectée. Cependant, si l’accentuation des contours améliore la lisibilité, la périphérie demeure assez floue, malgré une correction efficace de la distorsion. Le piqué diminue vers les bords et certaines zones claires sont légèrement surexposées.
Les prises de vue nocturnes restent exploitables grâce à un centre lisible et un piqué correct, mais les bords perdent en netteté et en précision. Si l'on observe des textures lissées, l'exposition et la distorsion typique de cette optique sont bien gérées. Les couleurs gardent leur naturel avec un bruit discret et sans aberrations disgracieuses.
Malgré une faible définition, le téléobjectif livre des clichés diurnes convaincants avec un piqué correct au centre et des inscriptions lisibles, mais la netteté baisse progressivement en périphérie. On note un léger renforcement logiciel visant à accentuer certains contours. Les couleurs restent fidèles, les contrastes équilibrés et l’exposition bien maîtrisée.
De nuit, en revanche, les photos sont difficilement exploitables, hormis pour un usage sur les réseaux sociaux. Le niveau de détail recule nettement, la faute à un lissage marqué qui ne parvient pas à effacer le bruit numérique encore bien présent. Les couleurs virent au chaud, la dynamique se montre limitée et on constate un léger vignettage de l'image.
Samsung abandonne les caméras sous l’écran et équipe les deux dalles du Z Fold 8 Ultra d’un capteur de 10 Mpx (f/2,2). La dynamique et le mode portrait sont réussis, malgré une définition limitée. Pour de meilleurs selfies, le mode arrière exploite le capteur principal avec retour sur le cover display. En vidéo, le smartphone filme jusqu’en 8K 30 i/s, propose une stabilisation très efficace en QHD à 60 i/s, et les capteurs frontaux montent jusqu’en 4K 60 i/s.
Pour conserver un boîtier aussi fin sans sacrifier l’endurance, Samsung adopte pour la première fois une batterie silicium-carbone. Déjà répandue chez plusieurs concurrents chinois, cette technologie augmente la densité énergétique et permet ici d’intégrer 5000 mAh dans un espace réduit. Ce choix marque un vrai tournant pour une marque longtemps prudente sur ce sujet depuis l'affaire Galaxy Note 7. Résultat : 21 h 27 min d’autonomie moyenne, avec 20 h 44 min écran ouvert et 22 h 9 min en utilisant uniquement le cover display.
La charge progresse elle aussi avec une puissance passant de 25 à 45 W en filaire. Il faut environ 56 min pour faire le plein, que le téléphone soit plié ou déplié. La charge sans-fil atteint quant à elle 20 W avec la compatibilité Qi2 Ready (sans aimants), tandis que la charge inversée (4,5 W) s’avère utile pour dépanner un accessoire en rade. Ce n’est pas encore une fusée au branchement, mais l’ensemble gagne enfin en cohérence avec le positionnement Ultra.
Notre score de durabilité permet de déterminer l'aspect durable du smartphone, autant pour le consommateur que pour l'environnement. Il s'appuie sur des éléments puisés dans l’étiquette énergie mise en place par l’Union européenne (classe énergétique, scores de résistance aux chutes et de réparabilité, nombre de cycles de batterie avant de tomber sous une capacité de 80 % et résistance de l’écran aux rayures). Nous y ajoutons des critères de durabilité (indice de protection IP, connecteurs standards, durée de garantie et des mises à jour…) et une évaluation des politiques RSE (Responsabilité sociétale des entreprises). Vous trouverez tous les détails de l'analyse dans notre article présentant notre score de durabilité.
Plus fin, plus puissant mais également plus cher, le Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra profite de deux écrans très lumineux, d’une pliure discrète, d’un volet photo polyvalent, de performances remarquables et d’un multitâche maîtrisé. Son autonomie solide, sa charge améliorée et son suivi logiciel longue durée renforcent encore l’ensemble. Quelques limites subsistent, notamment l’absence de S Pen, une étanchéité perfectible et quelques logiciels préinstallés. Une évolution très aboutie, davantage fondée sur le perfectionnement que sur la révolution, réservée au nouveau format de son petit frère.
Face aux Motorola Razr Fold et Honor Magic V6, le Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra mise d’abord sur sa légèreté, ses écrans nettement plus lumineux et une puissance mieux maîtrisée : il égale le Magic V6 sur le terrain du gaming, et distance le Razr Fold, handicapé par une puce moins véloce. Il cède toutefois sur l’endurance, domaine où le modèle de Motorola domine largement, ainsi que sur la charge et la robustesse face au V6.

articles.title: ChatGPT n'écrit plus à la manière de vos auteurs préférés
articles.text:
Pendant trois ans, imiter la plume d’un romancier célèbre a été l’un des tours favoris de ChatGPT, et l’un des plus pratiqués (les forums d’écriture regorgent de consignes toutes prêtes pour singer tel ou tel best-seller). L’exercice vient de prendre fin, sans annonce et sans explication, comme si l’éditeur du chatbot espérait que personne ne remarquerait rien.
Le chatbot décline, mais garde un plan B sous le coude
Les tests menés ces derniers jours convergent tous. Réclamez une scène d’ouverture à la manière de Stephen King, et la machine répond qu’elle ne peut imiter ni son « style exact » ni sa « voix distinctive ». Elle propose à la place un texte original construit sur l’angoisse de petite ville et la tension psychologique. Le refus vaut pour les vivants (J.K. Rowling, Amy Tan) comme pour les morts, Agatha Christie, Charles Dickens ou Ernest Hemingway. Pour la romancière britannique, la machine invoque même des œuvres « encore protégées par le droit d’auteur ».
Lire aussi : Scanner des livres pour entraîner son IA : c’est légal aux États-Unis, selon cette décision de justice inédite
Un audit indépendant publié quelques semaines plus tôt montrait pourtant le chatbot encore docile face aux demandes visant les auteurs décédés : le verrou a donc été posé ces dernières semaines, en silence. OpenAI, sollicité par Ars Technica (à l’origine de la découverte), n’a pas commenté. Les abonnés payants qui nourrissaient leurs propres romans avec la fonction ont déjà commencé à râler sur les forums (et on avoue un sourire en repensant à cette autrice de romance qui avait laissé traîner, dans un livre publié l’an dernier, sa consigne demandant de réécrire un passage à la manière d’une consœur du genre).
Le blocage a par ailleurs les épaules moins larges qu’il n’y paraît. Décrivez la recette sans prononcer le nom (narration orale, tension psychologique, bourgade qui cache un secret) et la machine s’exécute sans broncher. Il faut croire qu’il n’y a que la cybersécurité qui mérite de vrais gardes-fou
Quatre intelligences artificielles, quatre règles différentes
Le droit américain n’offre pourtant pas de réponse limpide : il protège l’expression d’une œuvre, pas le style d’un auteur en tant que tel. Une imitation ne devient contrefaçon que si le résultat s’avère substantiellement similaire à l’original. Ce flou n’a pas empêché les plaintes de s’empiler contre OpenAI, du New York Times à des romanciers de premier plan, les premiers ayant dégainé dès 2023.
Pourquoi de telles précautions de la part d’OpenAI ? La raison se trouve du côté de ses plus grands concurrents. Anthropic a accepté de verser 1,5 milliard de dollars aux auteurs américains, un accord définitivement validé par la justice le 20 juillet. La nuance que beaucoup de résumés écrasent mérite pourtant le détour. Le juge avait estimé l’entraînement sur des livres couvert par le fair use américain : c’est le téléchargement pirate de millions de copies qui a coûté le pactole. Autrement dit, le danger juridique ne porte pas sur ce que les modèles apprennent, mais sur ce qu’on leur a fait lire et sur ce qu’ils recrachent. D’où l’attention toute neuve portée aux sorties.
La concurrence, elle, n’a visiblement pas reçu le même mémo. Le même audit a comparé les politiques maison : Gemini s’exécute sans sourciller, Claude et Copilot obtempèrent en ajoutant un avertissement, et Perplexity refuse tout le monde, vivants comme morts. Quatre politiques différentes pour une même question juridique, ce qui dit surtout une chose : personne ne sait où passe la ligne, et chacun place le curseur selon son exposition aux tribunaux. Côté français, le style n’est pas davantage protégé en tant que tel, mais le droit moral et le parasitisme offrent aux auteurs des angles d’attaque que le fair use ignore.

articles.title: Smart #1 (2026) : nouvelle architecture 800 V et temps de recharge
articles.text:
Lancée en 2022 avec l’ambition de réinventer la marque sous l’impulsion du duo Mercedes-Benz (au design) et Geely (à la technique), la Smart #1 accuse le coup. En Chine, ses ventes se sont effondrées de près de 48 % au premier semestre 2026. Et en France, le bilan n’est guère plus réjouissant. Sa production en Chine la prive de bonus écologique. Un handicap tarifaire de taille face aux Fiat 600e, Skoda Elroq ou Volvo EX30.
Pour redonner un souffle à son modèle, Smart a décidé de revoir de fond en comble les entrailles électroniques de son véhicule. En attendant son officialisation, les premières informations ont déjà fuité sur les médias chinois comme CarNewsChina. Est-ce suffisant pour relancer la machine ?
10 à 80 % en 12 minutes : le bond technologique de la Smart #1
La mise à jour de la Smart #1 ne se contente pas d’un simple restylage cosmétique. Le modèle abandonne son architecture 400 V classique pour adopter une architecture 800 V. Les chiffres issus des fiches d’homologation chinoises sont assez aguicheurs :
- Un pic de charge à 370 kW (DC) : Grâce à sa nouvelle batterie de 61,5 kWh acceptant une recharge de type 6C, la Smart #1 peut encaisser une puissance équivalente à six fois la capacité de son pack.
- Le 10 à 80 % expédié en 12 minutes : Contre 30 minutes auparavant. Sur une station ultra-rapide compatible, le temps d’arrêt devient presque transparent pour le conducteur.
- Un nouveau moteur « 16-en-1 » plus puissant : Le #1 adopte un bloc électrique développé par Geely développant jusqu’à 245 kW (329 ch), avec une efficience annoncée à 93,8 %.
La vitesse de charge suffit-elle à compenser l’absence de bonus ?
En apportant les technologies de charge réservées jusqu’ici aux modèles haut de gamme (Porsche Taycan, Hyundai Ioniq 5 ou Mercedes CLA), la Smart #1 s’offre un rafraîchissement de sa fiche technique qui suscite l’intérêt.
Mais la question de sa carrière en France reste entière. Depuis l’instauration du score environnemental, la Smart #1 se voit privée de l’aide d’État (allant de 4 000 à 7 000 €) en raison de son empreinte carbone liée au transport depuis la Chine. Un coup dur face à des rivales assemblées en Europe qui tirent les prix vers le bas. En 2024, la Smart #1 a enregistré 1 241 immatriculations, elles n’étaient plus que 300 en 2025 et 143 pour le premier semestre 2026. Le reste du marché européen n’est guère plus réjouissant.
Sur le marché français, l’argument du « 10 à 80 % en 12 minutes » s’adresse avant tout aux gros rouleurs qui effectuent de fréquents trajets autoroutiers, ce qui n’est pas forcément la cible première de ce modèle.
Cette mise à jour technique s’accompagnera-t-elle d’un repositionnement tarifaire agressif de la part de Smart pour compenser la taxe sur les véhicules électriques chinois et l’absence d’aide d’État ? Lancement prévu en Chine le 6 août prochain, avant une arrivée attendue sur les routes européennes d’ici la fin de l’année.
